subject: Economy
stem:
Which of the following are the sources of income for the Reserve Bank of India ?
I. Buying and selling Government bonds
II. Buying and selling foreign currency
III. Pension fund management
IV. Lending to private companies
V. Printing and distributing currency notes

Select the correct answer using the code given below.

keywords.shortNote: The earnings derived by the central bank primarily from interest on domestic assets (G-Secs, LAF repos) and earnings on foreign currency assets (foreign sovereign bonds, deposits, exchange rate operations).
keywords.concept: RBI Sources of Income: The earnings derived by the central bank primarily from interest on domestic assets (G-Secs, LAF repos) and earnings on foreign currency assets (foreign sovereign bonds, deposits, exchange rate operations).

keywords.shortNote: While currency issuance carries seigniorage conceptually, printing, minting, and logistics under Section 25 of the RBI Act represent an operational expense paid to presses like BRBNMPL and SPMCIL, not a recurring operational income stream.
keywords.concept: Seigniorage & Currency Costs: While currency issuance carries seigniorage conceptually, printing, minting, and logistics under Section 25 of the RBI Act represent an operational expense paid to presses like BRBNMPL and SPMCIL, not a recurring operational income stream.

optionBreakdown.label: a
optionBreakdown.explanation: Statements I and II correctly identify the RBI's primary sources of domestic and foreign operational earnings. Statements III, IV, and V are either prohibited functions or net expenditure activities.

optionBreakdown.label: b
optionBreakdown.reference: Statements III and IV are statutorily false
optionBreakdown.explanation: RBI does not manage pension funds or lend directly to private enterprises.

optionBreakdown.label: c
optionBreakdown.reference: Statements III, IV, and V are false
optionBreakdown.explanation: Lumps together prohibited commercial activities and operational expenditure.

optionBreakdown.label: d
optionBreakdown.reference: Statement V is an expense, not income
optionBreakdown.explanation: Confuses the central bank function of currency issuance with an operational revenue source; printing and distribution is an explicit cost.

valueAddition.title: Anatomy of RBI's Profit & Loss Account
bullets: Gross Income Breakdown: Broadly split into Domestic Income and Foreign Income.

Domestic Sources: Interest income on holding of Government of India Dated Securities and Treasury Bills, net gains/losses on sale/redemption of securities, interest on liquidity adjustment facility (LAF) repos, and management commission for managing public debt.
Foreign Sources: Interest earned on foreign sovereign bonds and foreign central bank deposits, discount/exchange variations, and net trading profits on foreign currency sales.

Major Expenditure Heads: Agency charges paid to commercial banks for handling government business, printing of banknotes (payable to BRBNMPL and SPMCIL), employee compensation, and provisions transferred to the Contingency Fund (CF) and Asset Development Fund (ADF).

valueAddition.title: Surplus Transfer & The Bimal Jalan Committee (2019)
bullets: Section 47 of the RBI Act: Mandates that after making provisions for bad and doubtful debts, depreciation in assets, and staff superannuation funds, the balance surplus is transferred annually to the Central Government.

Bimal Jalan Framework: Recommended maintaining the Contingency Risk Buffer (CRB) within a band of 5.5% to 6.5% of the RBI's balance sheet, transferring the residual net surplus to the Ministry of Finance.

Revaluation Reserves: Currency and Gold Revaluation Account (CGRA) and Investment Revaluation Account (IRA) act as valuation buffers against market and exchange shocks and cannot be transferred as realized income.

valueAddition.title: Prohibited Activities of the RBI
bullets: Commercial Lending: Barred from engaging in trade, acquiring commercial equity shares, or granting direct advances to private commercial enterprises.
Immovable Property: Prohibited from purchasing immovable property except for its own official premises and staff residences.
Interest on Deposits: Barred from paying interest on current deposits held by scheduled banks under CRR mandates.

inNews.source: Reserve Bank of India / The Indian Express
inNews.headline: RBI Board Approves Annual Surplus Transfer to the Union Government Anchored by Higher Domestic and Foreign Asset Yields
inNews.relevance: Directly highlights the composition of RBI's surplus transfer under Section 47, demonstrating that rising interest on domestic G-Secs and global foreign exchange earnings drive the central bank's distributable profits.

statementBreakdown.reference: Sections 17(8) & 17(2) of RBI Act, 1934 / RBI Annual Report
statementBreakdown.explanation: Open Market Operations (OMOs), purchase/sale of government securities, and coupon/interest earnings on its domestic treasury portfolio constitute the largest domestic component of RBI's gross income.

Transactions in the foreign exchange market (buying/selling USD, EUR, etc.), foreign securities trading, and net gains/losses on foreign exchange transactions generate significant foreign earnings for the RBI.

Pension funds in India are managed by registered Pension Fund Managers (PFMs) regulated under PFRDA. The RBI is a central bank and macroeconomic regulator, not a commercial asset/pension fund manager.
The RBI acts as a 'banker to banks' and banker to the government. It is statutorily barred from directly lending to private commercial corporations or the general public.

statementBreakdown.reference: Expenditure Head: Currency and Coinage Expenses (RBI Balance Sheet)
statementBreakdown.explanation: Printing and distributing banknotes is an expenditure head for the RBI, involving procurement payments made to printing presses (BRBNMPL and SPMCIL), security paper mills, and transit charges.

visualSuggestion.title: RBI Balance Sheet: Realized Income vs. Operational Expenses

rows: Generates recurring coupon/interest and capital gains via OMOs
Yields interest on foreign treasuries and realized forex trading gains
Payments incurred for paper, ink, printing charges to presses, and security transit
Barred under Section 19 of the RBI Act to prevent commercial conflict and credit risk
Falls exclusively within the regulatory and operational jurisdiction of PFRDA/PFMs

hook.headline: How does the Reserve Bank of India actually make money?
hook.teaser: Don't say 'printing cash'—that is actually an expense, not an income.

keywords.calloutNote: Printing notes costs money; it is an expenditure paid to printing presses, not operational income.
activePhrases: Printing and distributing currency notes

keywords.calloutNote: Under Section 19 of the RBI Act, the central bank is barred from lending directly to commercial firms.
activePhrases: Lending to private companies
dimmedPhrases: Printing and distributing currency notes

verdicts.source: Interest on government dated securities and treasury bills is RBI's primary domestic revenue stream.
Returns on foreign treasury bonds and realized net gains from currency trading constitute foreign income.
Pension fund management is handled by commercial fund managers under PFRDA regulations.
RBI lends to banks and governments, never directly to private commercial corporations.
Paying BRBNMPL and SPMCIL for security paper and printing is an operating expenditure.

answer.label: A
answer.text: Only statements I and II are valid sources of income; III and IV are legally prohibited and V is an operational expense.

valueAddition.subtitle: Add these to your RBI Balance Sheet notes

items.title: Prohibited Business
items.desc: Prohibits the RBI from engaging in trade, holding real estate for commercial gain, or lending to private firms.

items.title: Surplus Transfer
items.desc: Profits remaining after statutory reserves and contingency buffers are transferred annually to the Government of India.

items.title: CRB Band
items.desc: Contingency Risk Buffer is pegged at 5.5% to 6.5% of the total balance sheet to absorb market risks.

valueAddition.note: Most aspirants fall for 'printing currency' thinking of seigniorage, but on the balance sheet, note printing is strictly an expenditure line item.

stem:
With reference to the Government of India, consider the following information :

Organization | Some of its functions | It works under
I. Directorate of Enforcement | Enforces the provisions of Fugitive Economic Offenders Act, 2018 | Internal Security Division-I, Ministry of Home Affairs
II. Directorate of Revenue Intelligence | Enforces the Provisions of the Customs Act, 1962 | Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance
III. Directorate General of Systems and Data Management | Carrying out big data analytics to assist tax officers for better policy and nabbing tax evaders | Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance

In how many of the above rows is the information correctly matched ?

keywords.shortNote: A specialized multi-disciplinary financial investigation agency operating under the Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance, responsible for enforcing PMLA (2002), FEMA (1999), and FEOA (2018).
keywords.concept: Directorate of Enforcement (ED): A specialized multi-disciplinary financial investigation agency operating under the Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance, responsible for enforcing PMLA (2002), FEMA (1999), and FEOA (2018).

keywords.shortNote: The apex intelligence and anti-smuggling agency functioning under the Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC), Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance, enforcing the Customs Act, 1962.
keywords.concept: Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI): The apex intelligence and anti-smuggling agency functioning under the Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC), Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance, enforcing the Customs Act, 1962.

keywords.term: Directorate General of Systems and Data Management (DG Systems)
keywords.shortNote: The apex technical directorate of CBIC under the Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance, leveraging big data analytics, AI/ML tools, and risk management systems (RMS) to curb duty evasion and improve tax compliance.
keywords.concept: Directorate General of Systems and Data Management (DG Systems): The apex technical directorate of CBIC under the Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance, leveraging big data analytics, AI/ML tools, and risk management systems (RMS) to curb duty evasion and improve tax compliance.

optionBreakdown.label: a

optionBreakdown.reference: Rows II and III are valid
optionBreakdown.explanation: Rows II and III are completely correct.

valueAddition.title: Enforcement Wings under Department of Revenue (Ministry of Finance)
bullets: Directorate of Enforcement (ED): Enforces three key economic statutes: (1) Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002 (PMLA); (2) Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999 (FEMA); and (3) Fugitive Economic Offenders Act, 2018 (FEOA).

Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI): Formed in 1957 as an attached office under CBIC; acts as the apex intelligence organization for customs violations, trade-based money laundering, wildlife trafficking, and narcotics enforcement under the NDPS Act.
Directorate General of GST Intelligence (DGGI): Apex intelligence organization under CBIC for detecting and prosecuting evasion of Goods and Services Tax (GST) and Central Excise.

Central Economic Intelligence Bureau (CEIB): Apex coordinating body under the Department of Revenue established to coordinate and facilitate intelligence sharing among various economic enforcement agencies.

valueAddition.title: DG Systems and Big Data Analytics in Revenue Administration
bullets: ADVAIT (Advanced Analytics in Indirect Taxation): An indigenous big data engine deployed by DG Systems under CBIC to perform predictive data analytics across direct tax (CBDT), indirect tax (CBIC), MCA, and banking data.
Project Insight (CBDT): Analogous data integration engine managed by the Income Tax Department under CBDT to track non-filers, high-value financial transactions, and undisclosed assets.
Risk Management System (RMS): Automates customs clearance by profiling cargo consignments to detect undervaluation and misclassification without manual intervention.

inNews.source: PIB / Ministry of Finance
inNews.headline: Department of Revenue enhances inter-agency coordination between ED, DRI, and DG Systems to curb fraudulent ITC syndicates
inNews.relevance: Directly links the investigative and data analytics collaboration across enforcement directorates operating under the Ministry of Finance.

statementBreakdown.reference: Government of India (Allocation of Business) Rules, 1961 · Department of Revenue
statementBreakdown.explanation: While the Directorate of Enforcement (ED) does enforce the Fugitive Economic Offenders Act, 2018 (FEOA) alongside PMLA and FEMA, it functions administratively under the Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance, not under the Ministry of Home Affairs.

The Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI) is the apex agency responsible for enforcing the Customs Act, 1962, intercepting smuggling, illicit trade, and commercial customs fraud, and functions under the Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC), Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance.

statementBreakdown.reference: CBIC Directorate General of Systems & Data Management Mandate
statementBreakdown.explanation: The Directorate General of Systems and Data Management (DG Systems) functions under the Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance (CBIC). It develops IT infrastructure, manages GSTN/Customs data integration, and deploys advanced big data analytics (such as ADVAIT) to identify red flags, combat fraudulent input tax credit (ITC), and trace tax evaders.

The Directorate of Revenue Intelligence enforces the Customs Act under CBIC, Ministry of Finance.
DG Systems leads big data analytics and automated tax compliance under the Department of Revenue.

stem:
Consider the following statements :
I. The Reserve Bank of India mandates all the listed companies in India to submit a Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report (BRSR).
II. In India, a company submitting a BRSR makes disclosures in the report that are largely non-financial in nature.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct ?

keywords.shortNote: A standardized reporting framework mandated by SEBI for listed entities to disclose their environmental, social, and governance (ESG) performance.
keywords.concept: Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report: A standardized reporting framework mandated by SEBI for listed entities to disclose their environmental, social, and governance (ESG) performance.

keywords.shortNote: Corporate reporting on metrics outside conventional balance-sheet accounting, covering carbon emissions, employee well-being, diversity, and ethical supply chains.
keywords.concept: Non-Financial Disclosures: Corporate reporting on metrics outside conventional balance-sheet accounting, covering carbon emissions, employee well-being, diversity, and ethical supply chains.

keywords.shortNote: The primary capital-market framework governing continuous listing obligations, disclosure benchmarks, and corporate governance for publicly traded firms in India.
keywords.concept: SEBI LODR Regulations: The primary capital-market framework governing continuous listing obligations, disclosure benchmarks, and corporate governance for publicly traded firms in India.

optionBreakdown.label: a
optionBreakdown.explanation: Attributes listing compliance to the central bank rather than the capital markets regulator (SEBI).

optionBreakdown.label: b
optionBreakdown.explanation: Statement II correctly identifies the non-financial ESG nature of BRSR disclosures, while Statement I wrongly names the regulator.

optionBreakdown.label: c
optionBreakdown.explanation: Overlooks the statutory distinction between RBI (banking and monetary regulator) and SEBI (stock market and listing regulator).

optionBreakdown.label: d
optionBreakdown.explanation: Incorrectly rejects Statement II, which accurately characterizes the reporting substance of the BRSR framework.

valueAddition.title: Evolution of BRSR Reporting in India
bullets: Originates from the National Voluntary Guidelines (2011) and updated National Guidelines on Responsible Business Conduct (NGRBC, 2019) anchored on 9 core principles.
In May 2021, SEBI replaced the earlier Business Responsibility Report (BRR) with the more comprehensive and quantitative BRSR framework.
Applicable mandatorily to the top 1,000 listed companies by market capitalization from financial year 2022-23 onwards.

valueAddition.title: BRSR Core & Value Chain Assurance
bullets: SEBI introduced 'BRSR Core', a subset of Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) requiring reasonable assurance by independent assurance providers.
Extends ESG surveillance to value chains, requiring top listed companies to obtain disclosures from their key value chain partners (suppliers and distributors).
Aims to curb greenwashing in ESG mutual fund schemes by tying sustainable asset allocation directly to verified BRSR Core performance.

inNews.source: Securities and Exchange Board of India Circular
inNews.headline: SEBI Streamlines Value Chain Disclosures and Assurance Norms for BRSR Core Across Top 250 Listed Firms
inNews.relevance: Refined compliance norms ease reporting bottlenecks for small vendors while ensuring audited environmental and workplace safety disclosures across major corporate supply chains.

statementBreakdown.explanation: The mandate comes from the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI), not the Reserve Bank of India. SEBI requires the top 1,000 listed entities by market capitalization to submit a BRSR as part of their annual reports.
BRSR centers on ESG metrics—greenhouse gas emissions, water stewardship, waste recycling, workforce safety, consumer grievance redressal, and anti-corruption—which are non-financial disclosures.

subject: Economy
stem:
Consider the following statements :
Statement I : As regards returns from an investment in a company, generally, bondholders are considered to be relatively at lower risk than stockholders.
Statement II : Bondholders are lenders to a company whereas stockholders are its owners.
Statement III : For repayment purpose, bondholders are prioritized over stockholders by a company.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements ?

options.text: Both Statement II and Statement III are correct and both of them explain Statement I
options.label: a

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement I explains Statement II
options.label: b

options.text: Only one of the Statements II and III is correct and that explains Statement I
options.label: c

options.text: Neither Statement II nor Statement III is correct
options.label: d

keywords.shortNote: The specific combination of debt (borrowed capital via bonds/debentures) and equity (ownership capital via shares) used by a corporate entity to finance overall operations and growth.
keywords.concept: Capital Structure: The specific combination of debt (borrowed capital via bonds/debentures) and equity (ownership capital via shares) used by a corporate entity to finance overall operations and growth.

keywords.shortNote: The statutory order of repayment priority established by corporate law and bankruptcy frameworks, mandating that debt obligations must be satisfied before any residual value is returned to equity shareholders.
keywords.concept: Creditor Hierarchy: The statutory order of repayment priority established by corporate law and bankruptcy frameworks, mandating that debt obligations must be satisfied before any residual value is returned to equity shareholders.

keywords.shortNote: An equity stockholder whose financial claim on corporate earnings and liquidation assets arises only after all contractual operational expenses, taxes, and debt servicing obligations have been completely paid.
keywords.concept: Residual Claimant: An equity stockholder whose financial claim on corporate earnings and liquidation assets arises only after all contractual operational expenses, taxes, and debt servicing obligations have been completely paid.

optionBreakdown.label: a
optionBreakdown.explanation: Statements II and III are both accurate legal and financial premises that together explain why bondholders face lower risk (Statement I): bondholders are external lenders (II) whose repayment claims strictly precede equity owners (III).

optionBreakdown.label: b
optionBreakdown.explanation: Reverses the direction of economic causation; a lower risk profile does not create the legal status of being a lender—rather, being a lender creates the lower risk profile.

optionBreakdown.label: c
optionBreakdown.explanation: Incorrectly asserts that either Statement II or Statement III is untrue, whereas both are verified legal and operational facts.

optionBreakdown.label: d
optionBreakdown.explanation: Disregards established commercial law and bankruptcy codes regarding creditor status and liquidation priority.

valueAddition.title: Why Debt Carries Lower Risk than Equity
bullets: Contractual Claim vs Residual Claim: Bond interest constitutes a mandatory charge on profit (pre-tax expense) that must be paid regardless of whether the company records a profit or a loss.
Dividends: Dividends paid to equity stockholders represent an optional appropriation of profit (post-tax), decided at the discretion of the Board of Directors.
Legal Ownership: Stockholders bear the ultimate downside business risk as proprietors, compensated by voting control and uncapped upside capital gains.

valueAddition.title: Repayment Priority Under the Insolvency Waterfall
bullets: Section 53 of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC), 2016 governs the distribution of liquidation proceeds through a mandatory waterfall mechanism.
Secured and unsecured financial creditors (including bondholders and debenture holders) sit near the top of the recovery ladder.
Equity shareholders occupy the bottom rank of the waterfall, receiving payouts only if surplus capital remains after all creditor classes are settled.

inNews.relevance: Resolution outcomes under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code consistently demonstrate debt priority, as corporate turnaround plans settled senior bondholder claims while writing down equity shares to zero.

statementBreakdown.explanation: Bondholders carry lower investment return risk because their coupons are contractual fixed obligations paid before taxes, whereas stockholders receive volatile, non-guaranteed dividends dependent entirely on residual profits.

Bondholders hold debt instruments and stand legally as creditors (lenders) entitled to fixed periodic interest and principal redemption, whereas equity stockholders hold fractional proprietary shares as owners.
Under both standard ongoing solvency and formal corporate liquidation, contractual debt claims of bondholders must be serviced before any capital can be distributed to equity owners.

subject: Economy
stem:
Consider the following statements :
I. Capital receipts create a liability or cause a reduction in the assets of the Government.
II. Borrowings and disinvestment are capital receipts.
III. Interest received on loans creates a liability of the Government.

Which of the statements given above are correct ?

keywords.shortNote: All government receipts that either create a future repayment liability (such as market borrowings) or reduce financial assets of the government (such as disinvestment proceeds or loan recoveries).
keywords.concept: Capital Receipts: All government receipts that either create a future repayment liability (such as market borrowings) or reduce financial assets of the government (such as disinvestment proceeds or loan recoveries).

keywords.shortNote: Recurring government receipts—comprising tax revenues and non-tax revenues like interest, dividends, and fees—that neither create any liability nor cause a reduction in government assets.
keywords.concept: Revenue Receipts: Recurring government receipts—comprising tax revenues and non-tax revenues like interest, dividends, and fees—that neither create any liability nor cause a reduction in government assets.

keywords.shortNote: The sale or liquidation of government equity shareholding in Central Public Sector Enterprises (CPSEs), classified as a non-debt capital receipt because it reduces the government's financial assets.
keywords.concept: Disinvestment: The sale or liquidation of government equity shareholding in Central Public Sector Enterprises (CPSEs), classified as a non-debt capital receipt because it reduces the government's financial assets.

keywords.shortNote: Capital receipts that do not add to the government's debt burden, consisting primarily of disinvestment proceeds and recovery of loans previously extended by the government.
keywords.concept: Non-Debt Capital Receipts: Capital receipts that do not add to the government's debt burden, consisting primarily of disinvestment proceeds and recovery of loans previously extended by the government.

optionBreakdown.label: a
optionBreakdown.explanation: Accurately captures the definition and examples of capital receipts while excluding interest income, which is a revenue receipt.

optionBreakdown.label: b
optionBreakdown.explanation: Wrongly classifies interest earned by the government as a liability-creating transaction.

optionBreakdown.label: c
optionBreakdown.explanation: Fails to distinguish interest income (non-tax revenue) from principal loan recovery (non-debt capital receipt).

optionBreakdown.label: d
optionBreakdown.explanation: Overlooks the core accounting rule that revenue receipts create zero liabilities.

valueAddition.title: The Two-Question Accounting Test for Any Budget Receipt
bullets: Ask two questions about any rupee entering the government treasury: (1) Does it create a future repayment liability? (2) Does it reduce an existing government asset?
If the answer to either question is YES, it is a Capital Receipt—borrowings fail test 1 (create liability), while disinvestment and recovery of loan principal fail test 2 (reduce assets).
If the answer to BOTH questions is NO, it is a Revenue Receipt—taxes, dividends from RBI/PSUs, user fees, and interest received on loans leave assets and liabilities untouched.

valueAddition.title: Loan Principal Recovery vs. Interest Received
bullets: When a State government repays the principal of a central loan, the Centre's financial asset (loan receivable) shrinks—so principal recovery is a Non-Debt Capital Receipt.
When that same State pays annual interest on the loan, the principal loan asset remains intact and no new liability arises—so interest received is strictly a Non-Tax Revenue Receipt.

inNews.source: Ministry of Finance / DIPAM
inNews.headline: Centre Mobilizes Non-Debt Capital Receipts Through Strategic Stake Sales and CPSE Dividends
inNews.relevance: Department of Investment and Public Asset Management (DIPAM) data in October 2026 highlighted steady disinvestment inflows alongside record RBI and PSU dividend transfers bolstering non-tax revenue receipts.

statementBreakdown.explanation: By strict accounting definition, any inflow into the Consolidated Fund of India that either creates a debt liability or reduces existing government assets is classified as a capital receipt.

Market borrowings create a repayment liability (debt capital receipt), while disinvestment reduces the government's equity ownership in CPSEs (non-debt capital receipt)—making both standard capital receipts.

Interest received by the government on loans extended to States, UTs, or PSUs is a recurring non-tax revenue receipt that neither creates a liability nor reduces the principal loan asset (only principal recovery reduces the asset).

hook.headline: Does interest received by the government create a liability?
hook.teaser: Notice how UPSC pulls two textbook NCERT lines and slips in one classic accounting trap in Statement III.

keywords.term: create a liability or cause a reduction in the assets
keywords.calloutTerm: “create a liability or cause a reduction in the assets”
keywords.calloutNote: That is the exact two-part NCERT definition of a capital receipt—if neither happens, it is a revenue receipt.
activePhrases: create a liability or cause a reduction in the assets

keywords.calloutNote: Do not confuse interest earned with loan recovery—receiving interest is regular income (revenue receipt), not a liability.
activePhrases: Interest received on loans
dimmedPhrases: create a liability or cause a reduction in the assets

verdicts.source: Capital receipts are defined specifically as government inflows that either create a repayment liability or reduce government assets.
Borrowings create a debt liability and disinvestment reduces government equity assets, making both textbook capital receipts.
Interest received on loans is regular non-tax revenue income—it neither creates a liability for the government nor reduces the loan principal.

answer.label: A
answer.text: Statements I and II give the exact NCERT definition and examples of capital receipts, while III is false—making Option A right.

valueAddition.title: Value addition
valueAddition.subtitle: Add these to your Budget & Fiscal Policy notes

items.title: Principal vs. Interest
items.desc: Recovery of loan principal reduces an asset (Capital Receipt), while interest received on that loan is pure income (Revenue Receipt).

items.title: Debt vs. Non-Debt Capital
items.desc: Borrowings are debt capital receipts; disinvestment and loan recoveries are non-debt capital receipts.

items.title: Dividends Are Revenue
items.desc: Surplus transfers from RBI and dividends from PSUs neither create debt nor sell equity, so they count as non-tax revenue.

valueAddition.note: Examiners routinely swap 'recovery of loans' (capital receipt) with 'interest received on loans' (revenue receipt) because both come from borrowers.

subject: Economy
stem:
Suppose the revenue expenditure is ₹ 80,000 crores and the revenue receipts of the Government are ₹ 60,000 crores. The Government budget also shows borrowings of ₹ 10,000 crores and interest payments of ₹ 6,000 crores. Which of the following statements are correct ?
I. Revenue deficit is ₹ 20,000 crores.
II. Fiscal deficit is ₹ 10,000 crores.
III. Primary deficit is ₹ 4,000 crores.

Select the correct answer using the code given below.

keywords.shortNote: The excess of a government's total revenue expenditure over its total revenue receipts during a fiscal year, indicating dissaving on the current consumption account.
keywords.concept: Revenue Deficit: The excess of a government's total revenue expenditure over its total revenue receipts during a fiscal year, indicating dissaving on the current consumption account.

keywords.shortNote: The excess of total budget expenditure over total non-debt receipts during a financial year, which is numerically equal to the net total borrowing requirement of the government.
keywords.concept: Fiscal Deficit: The excess of total budget expenditure over total non-debt receipts during a financial year, which is numerically equal to the net total borrowing requirement of the government.

keywords.shortNote: Fiscal deficit minus interest payments on accumulated past debt, isolating how much of current borrowing goes toward fresh non-interest expenditure rather than servicing old loans.
keywords.concept: Primary Deficit: Fiscal deficit minus interest payments on accumulated past debt, isolating how much of current borrowing goes toward fresh non-interest expenditure rather than servicing old loans.

optionBreakdown.label: a
optionBreakdown.explanation: Misses the straightforward subtraction of interest payments (Rs. 6,000 crores) from fiscal deficit (Rs. 10,000 crores).

optionBreakdown.label: b
optionBreakdown.explanation: Overlooks the direct Revenue Deficit calculation of Rs. 20,000 crores.

optionBreakdown.label: c
optionBreakdown.explanation: Fails to recognize that Fiscal Deficit is identical to total government borrowings (Rs. 10,000 crores).

optionBreakdown.label: d
optionBreakdown.explanation: All three calculations follow the exact NCERT and Union Budget deficit identities.

valueAddition.title: The Three Core Budget Deficit Identities
bullets: Revenue Deficit = Revenue Expenditure - Revenue Receipts (measures day-to-day operational shortfall).

Fiscal Deficit = Total Expenditure - Non-Debt Receipts = Total Borrowings (measures overall borrowing requirement; note that Fiscal Deficit can be smaller than Revenue Deficit if non-debt capital receipts like disinvestment exceed capital expenditure).
Primary Deficit = Fiscal Deficit - Interest Payments (shows whether current borrowing is funding fresh developmental spending or merely paying interest on inherited debt).

valueAddition.title: Effective Revenue Deficit (ERD) & Policy Intuition
bullets: Effective Revenue Deficit = Revenue Deficit - Grants for Creation of Capital Assets (introduced in Budget 2011–12 because central grants to States/UTs for building roads or schools are booked as revenue expenditure in the Centre's accounts despite creating physical assets).
When Primary Deficit approaches zero, the government is borrowing solely to service interest obligations on past debt rather than expanding new public services.

inNews.source: Controller General of Accounts (CGA) / Business Standard
inNews.headline: Centre's Fiscal Deficit Reaches 29.4% of Full-Year Target in H1 FY27 Amid Strong Tax Buoyancy
inNews.relevance: CGA monthly fiscal accounts released in October 2026 showed contained revenue deficit and steady net market borrowings, keeping India's primary deficit and debt-to-GDP consolidation path on track.

statementBreakdown.reference: NCERT Class XII Macroeconomics — Budget Deficits
statementBreakdown.explanation: Revenue Deficit = Revenue Expenditure - Revenue Receipts = Rs. 80,000 crores - Rs. 60,000 crores = Rs. 20,000 crores.

By accounting definition, Fiscal Deficit equals the total net borrowings of the government during the year—which is explicitly given in the budget data as Rs. 10,000 crores (implying a capital account surplus of Rs. 10,000 crores from non-debt capital receipts offsetting part of the revenue deficit).
Primary Deficit = Fiscal Deficit - Interest Payments = Rs. 10,000 crores - Rs. 6,000 crores = Rs. 4,000 crores.

visualSuggestion.title: Step-by-Step Calculation of Budget Deficit Indicators

rows: Directly equal to Borrowings = Rs. 10,000 crores

hook.headline: Can a government's Fiscal Deficit ever be smaller than its Revenue Deficit?
hook.teaser: Notice how UPSC tests three classic NCERT budget formulas in one clean numerical question.

keywords.calloutNote: Remember the golden accounting rule: Fiscal Deficit is always equal to total government borrowings.
activePhrases: borrowings of ₹ 10,000 crores

keywords.calloutNote: Subtract interest payments directly from the Fiscal Deficit to isolate the Primary Deficit.
activePhrases: interest payments of ₹ 6,000 crores
dimmedPhrases: borrowings of ₹ 10,000 crores
contextPhrases: revenue receipts of the Government are ₹ 60,000 crores

verdicts.source: Revenue Deficit is simply Revenue Expenditure minus Revenue Receipts, which gives Rs. 80,000 minus Rs. 60,000 = Rs. 20,000 crores.
By Union Budget accounting identity, Fiscal Deficit equals net total borrowings—which is stated directly as Rs. 10,000 crores.
Primary Deficit equals Fiscal Deficit minus Interest Payments: Rs. 10,000 crores minus Rs. 6,000 crores = Rs. 4,000 crores.

answer.label: D
answer.text: All three NCERT deficit formulas check out cleanly—so I, II and III is the right answer.

valueAddition.title: Value addition
valueAddition.subtitle: Add these to your Budget & Fiscal Policy notes

items.title: Fiscal Deficit = Borrowings
items.desc: Whenever a question gives total borrowings, you already have the exact Fiscal Deficit without needing total expenditure.

items.title: Primary Deficit Meaning
items.desc: Primary Deficit (Fiscal Deficit minus Interest Payments) reveals how much fresh debt funds current spending rather than old interest.

items.title: Revenue > Fiscal Possible
items.desc: If non-debt capital receipts like disinvestment exceed capital spending, Fiscal Deficit can be lower than Revenue Deficit.

valueAddition.note: Many aspirants panic when Revenue Deficit (Rs. 20,000 cr) looks larger than Borrowings (Rs. 10,000 cr)—trust the textbook identity that Fiscal Deficit always equals Borrowings.

subject: Economy
stem: A country's fiscal deficit stands at ₹ 50,000 crores. It is receiving ₹ 10,000 crores through non-debt creating capital receipts. The country's interest liabilities are ₹ 1,500 crores. What is the gross primary deficit ?

keywords.shortNote: The excess of total government expenditure (revenue expenditure plus capital expenditure and net lending) over revenue receipts and non-debt creating capital receipts.
keywords.concept: Gross Fiscal Deficit: The excess of total government expenditure (revenue expenditure plus capital expenditure and net lending) over revenue receipts and non-debt creating capital receipts.

keywords.shortNote: Gross fiscal deficit minus gross interest payments on accumulated public debt, isolating the current fiscal year's borrowing requirement excluding past debt-servicing obligations.
keywords.concept: Gross Primary Deficit: Gross fiscal deficit minus gross interest payments on accumulated public debt, isolating the current fiscal year's borrowing requirement excluding past debt-servicing obligations.

keywords.shortNote: Capital receipts that do not increase the government's debt burden—such as disinvestment proceeds and recovery of loans—which are already netted out when computing the fiscal deficit.
keywords.concept: Non-Debt Creating Capital Receipts: Capital receipts that do not increase the government's debt burden—such as disinvestment proceeds and recovery of loans—which are already netted out when computing the fiscal deficit.

optionBreakdown.label: a
optionBreakdown.explanation: Gross Primary Deficit = Gross Fiscal Deficit - Interest Payments = Rs. 50,000 crores - Rs. 1,500 crores = Rs. 48,500 crores. Non-debt creating capital receipts (Rs. 10,000 crores) are already accounted for inside the given fiscal deficit figure.

optionBreakdown.label: b
optionBreakdown.explanation: Results from erroneously adding interest liabilities (Rs. 1,500 crores) to the fiscal deficit instead of subtracting them.

optionBreakdown.label: c
optionBreakdown.explanation: Results from adding Rs. 10,000 crores of non-debt capital receipts back into the fiscal deficit (50,000 + 10,000 - 1,500), double-counting an item already netted out.

optionBreakdown.label: d
optionBreakdown.explanation: Rs. 48,500 crores is explicitly listed as Option (a).

valueAddition.title: Why Non-Debt Capital Receipts Are Redundant Once Fiscal Deficit Is Given
bullets: By definition, Gross Fiscal Deficit = Total Expenditure - (Revenue Receipts + Non-Debt Creating Capital Receipts).

Because non-debt creating capital receipts (disinvestment and loan recoveries) have already been subtracted to arrive at the Rs. 50,000 crore fiscal deficit, adding or subtracting them again double-counts the figure.
Gross Primary Deficit then strips out only past debt servicing: Gross Primary Deficit = Gross Fiscal Deficit - Interest Payments (50,000 - 1,500 = Rs. 48,500 crores).

valueAddition.title: Gross vs. Net Fiscal and Primary Deficit (RBI Convention)
bullets: Gross Fiscal Deficit includes net lending by the Centre to States/PSUs on the expenditure side; Net Fiscal Deficit deducts net lending from Gross Fiscal Deficit.
Similarly, Gross Primary Deficit = Gross Fiscal Deficit - Gross Interest Payments, whereas Net Primary Deficit = Net Fiscal Deficit - Net Interest Payments (interest paid minus interest received).

inNews.source: Ministry of Finance / RBI Handbook of Statistics
inNews.headline: Centre Targets Primary Deficit Below 1.5% of GDP to Stabilize Public Debt Trajectory
inNews.relevance: Union Finance Ministry fiscal projections reviewed in September 2026 emphasized compressing the gross primary deficit toward zero so incremental market borrowings fund capital creation rather than debt interest.

visualSuggestion.title: Decoy Check: What Goes Into Gross Primary Deficit?

rows: Starting baseline (already nets out revenue & non-debt capital receipts)
Decoy data—already factored into the Rs. 50,000 cr fiscal deficit
Subtracted from Gross Fiscal Deficit (50,000 - 1,500 = Rs. 48,500 cr)

hook.headline: Why is the ₹ 10,000 crore figure in this UPSC math question a decoy?
hook.teaser: Notice how UPSC slips extra budget data into a two-line formula to bait you into double-counting.

keywords.calloutNote: Ignore this Rs. 10,000 crore figure—non-debt capital receipts are already subtracted when calculating the Rs. 50,000 crore fiscal deficit.
activePhrases: non-debt creating capital receipts

keywords.calloutNote: Simply take Gross Fiscal Deficit (50,000) minus Interest Liabilities (1,500) to get Rs. 48,500 crores.
activePhrases: gross primary deficit
dimmedPhrases: non-debt creating capital receipts

verdicts.source: Gross Primary Deficit equals Gross Fiscal Deficit minus Interest Liabilities: Rs. 50,000 crores minus Rs. 1,500 crores = Rs. 48,500 crores.
Rs. 51,500 crores comes from adding interest payments instead of subtracting them.
Rs. 58,500 crores wrongly adds Rs. 10,000 crores of non-debt capital receipts back into a fiscal deficit that already excluded them.
The exact answer Rs. 48,500 crores sits right in Option (a).

answer.label: A
answer.text: Ignore the Rs. 10,000 crore decoy and subtract Rs. 1,500 crore interest from Rs. 50,000 crore fiscal deficit—Option A is Rs. 48,500 crores.

valueAddition.title: Value addition
valueAddition.subtitle: Add these to your Budget & Fiscal Policy notes

items.title: Gross Primary Deficit
items.desc: Gross Primary Deficit = Gross Fiscal Deficit - Interest Payments (no adjustment needed for non-debt capital receipts).

items.title: Already Netted Out
items.desc: Fiscal Deficit already deducts both revenue receipts and non-debt capital receipts (disinvestment, loan recoveries) from total spending.

items.title: What Zero Primary Deficit Means
items.desc: If Primary Deficit is zero, the government is borrowing purely to pay interest on old loans, not for new spending.

valueAddition.note: Examiners put Rs. 58,500 crores in Option (c) specifically for candidates who mechanically add the Rs. 10,000 crore non-debt capital receipt figure.

subject: Economy
stem:
Which of the following statements with regard to recommendations of the 15th Finance Commission of India are correct ?
I. It has recommended grants of ₹ 4,800 crores from the year 2022-23 to the year 2025-26 for incentivizing States to enhance educational outcomes.
II. 45% of the net proceeds of Union taxes are to be shared with States.
III. ₹ 45,000 crores are to be kept as performance-based incentive for all States for carrying out agricultural reforms.
IV. It reintroduced tax effort criteria to reward fiscal performance.

Select the correct answer using the code given below.

keywords.shortNote: The percentage share of the net proceeds of central divisible taxes allocated collectively to State governments by the Finance Commission, set at 41% by the 15th Finance Commission for 2021–26.
keywords.concept: Vertical Devolution: The percentage share of the net proceeds of central divisible taxes allocated collectively to State governments by the Finance Commission, set at 41% by the 15th Finance Commission for 2021–26.

keywords.shortNote: The multi-parameter formula used by the Finance Commission to distribute the States' collective tax share among individual States based on equity, needs, demographic performance, and fiscal effort.
keywords.concept: Horizontal Devolution Formula: The multi-parameter formula used by the Finance Commission to distribute the States' collective tax share among individual States based on equity, needs, demographic performance, and fiscal effort.

keywords.shortNote: A horizontal devolution parameter carrying 2.5% weight in the 15th Finance Commission formula, rewarding States with higher tax collection efficiency relative to their Gross State Domestic Product.
keywords.concept: Tax and Fiscal Efforts Criterion: A horizontal devolution parameter carrying 2.5% weight in the 15th Finance Commission formula, rewarding States with higher tax collection efficiency relative to their Gross State Domestic Product.

keywords.shortNote: Conditional fiscal transfers recommended by the Finance Commission tied to verifiable State-level sectoral outcomes in agriculture, school education, aspirational districts, and power sector reforms.
keywords.concept: Performance-Based Grants: Conditional fiscal transfers recommended by the Finance Commission tied to verifiable State-level sectoral outcomes in agriculture, school education, aspirational districts, and power sector reforms.

optionBreakdown.label: a
optionBreakdown.explanation: Wrongly accepts 45% vertical tax devolution instead of the actual 41%.

optionBreakdown.label: b
optionBreakdown.explanation: Fails to catch the altered 45% vertical devolution figure.

optionBreakdown.label: c
optionBreakdown.explanation: Eliminating Statement II (45% vs. actual 41%) immediately isolates Option (c) as the sole valid combination.

optionBreakdown.label: d
optionBreakdown.explanation: Overlooks that 45% is factually false and omits the genuine Rs. 4,800 crore education grant.

valueAddition.title: 15th Finance Commission Horizontal Devolution Weights (2021–26)
bullets: Income Distance: 45% (gap between a State's per capita GSDP and that of the highest-income State, favoring equity).
Population (2011 Census): 15% and Area: 15% (15th FC shifted exclusively to 2011 Census data as mandated by its Terms of Reference).

Demographic Performance: 12.5% (rewarding States that lowered Total Fertility Rates), Forest & Ecology: 10% (up from 7.5% in 14th FC), and Tax & Fiscal Efforts: 2.5% (reintroduced to reward revenue mobilization).

valueAddition.title: Why Vertical Devolution Moved from 42% to 41%
bullets: The 14th Finance Commission had fixed States' vertical share at 42% when Jammu & Kashmir was a full-fledged State.

Following the Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Act, 2019, the 15th FC carved out 1% from the divisible pool to meet the fiscal needs of the Union Territories of J&K and Ladakh directly from the Centre, setting States' share at 41%.

inNews.source: 16th Finance Commission / Ministry of Finance
inNews.headline: States Seek Retention of Demographic Performance and Tax Effort Weights Under 16th Finance Commission
inNews.relevance: During consultations in October 2026, southern and industrialized States urged the 16th Finance Commission to raise the weightage of the 15th FC's Tax Effort and Demographic Performance criteria.

statementBreakdown.explanation: The 15th Finance Commission recommended Rs. 4,800 crores (Rs. 1,200 crores per year from 2022–23 to 2025–26) as performance-based grants to incentivize States to improve school education outcomes.

The 15th Finance Commission recommended sharing 41%—not 45%—of the net proceeds of Union taxes with States (maintaining the 14th FC's 42% level minus 1% adjusted for the newly created Union Territories of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh).

statementBreakdown.explanation: The Commission earmarked Rs. 45,000 crores as performance-based incentives across all States for undertaking agricultural reforms, including amendment of APMC laws, land leasing, contract farming, and groundwater conservation.

statementBreakdown.reference: 15th Finance Commission Report — Horizontal Devolution Weights
statementBreakdown.explanation: After the 14th Finance Commission had dropped tax/fiscal discipline parameters, the 15th Finance Commission reintroduced 'Tax and Fiscal Efforts' with a 2.5% weight to reward States demonstrating higher own-tax revenue efficiency.

keywords.calloutTerm: “45% of the net proceeds of Union taxes”
keywords.calloutNote: Here is the catch: 45% was the weight of Income Distance, whereas vertical tax devolution to States was 41%.

The 15th FC reintroduced Tax and Fiscal Efforts at 2.5% weight to reward States with strong own-tax collection efficiency.

subject: Economy
stem:
Consider the following statements in respect of the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD) :
I. It provides loans and guarantees to middle income countries.
II. It works single-handedly to help developing countries to reduce poverty.
III. It was established to help Europe rebuild after the World War II.

Which of the statements given above are correct ?

keywords.term: International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD)
keywords.shortNote: The original lending arm of the World Bank Group established at the 1944 Bretton Woods Conference that provides non-concessional loans, guarantees, risk management products, and advisory services to middle-income and creditworthy low-income countries.
keywords.concept: International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD): The original lending arm of the World Bank Group established at the 1944 Bretton Woods Conference that provides non-concessional loans, guarantees, risk management products, and advisory services to middle-income and creditworthy low-income countries.

keywords.shortNote: A multilateral development partnership comprising five distinct institutions—IBRD, IDA, IFC, MIGA, and ICSID—that coordinate sovereign lending, concessional aid, private-sector financing, political risk insurance, and investment dispute settlement.
keywords.concept: World Bank Group: A multilateral development partnership comprising five distinct institutions—IBRD, IDA, IFC, MIGA, and ICSID—that coordinate sovereign lending, concessional aid, private-sector financing, political risk insurance, and investment dispute settlement.

keywords.shortNote: The soft-loan window of the World Bank established in 1960 that provides zero-to-low-interest concessional credits and grants specifically to the world's poorest countries.
keywords.concept: International Development Association (IDA): The soft-loan window of the World Bank established in 1960 that provides zero-to-low-interest concessional credits and grants specifically to the world's poorest countries.

keywords.shortNote: The July 1944 United Nations Monetary and Financial Conference in New Hampshire that created the IBRD and the International Monetary Fund (IMF) to finance post-World War II reconstruction and stabilize global monetary cooperation.
keywords.concept: Bretton Woods Conference (1944): The July 1944 United Nations Monetary and Financial Conference in New Hampshire that created the IBRD and the International Monetary Fund (IMF) to finance post-World War II reconstruction and stabilize global monetary cooperation.

optionBreakdown.label: a
optionBreakdown.explanation: Accepts the false 'single-handedly' claim while overlooking IBRD's founding post-WWII European reconstruction role.

optionBreakdown.label: b
optionBreakdown.explanation: Misses IBRD's core modern lending role for middle-income countries while retaining the extreme 'single-handedly' qualifier.

optionBreakdown.label: c
optionBreakdown.explanation: Accurately pairs IBRD's historical post-WWII reconstruction mandate with its modern role extending loans and guarantees to middle-income countries, while rejecting the false 'single-handedly' claim.

optionBreakdown.label: d
optionBreakdown.explanation: Fails to eliminate the extreme adverb 'single-handedly', which contradicts the collaborative multi-agency structure of the World Bank Group.

valueAddition.title: How the Five World Bank Group Arms Divide Development Work
bullets: IBRD (1944) + IDA (1960) together form 'The World Bank': IBRD provides market-linked loans and guarantees to middle-income and creditworthy nations (like India), whereas IDA provides concessional zero/low-interest credits and grants to the poorest countries.

Three Complementary Affiliates: International Finance Corporation (IFC, 1956) finances private-sector projects; Multilateral Investment Guarantee Agency (MIGA, 1988) offers cross-border political risk insurance; and ICSID (1966) settles investor-state disputes (India is a member of IBRD, IDA, IFC, and MIGA, but not ICSID).

valueAddition.title: How IBRD Funds Its Loans Without Relying Only on Member Budgets
bullets: Member countries pay in only a small fraction of their subscribed capital while the rest acts as callable backing—enabling IBRD to borrow cheaply in global bond markets with a AAA rating and pass those low borrowing costs on to middle-income borrowers.

inNews.source: World Bank / Ministry of Finance
inNews.headline: World Bank Annual Meetings Expand IBRD Sovereign Guarantee Capacity and Hybrid Capital Instruments for Emerging Economies
inNews.relevance: October 2026 World Bank Group reforms expanded IBRD's balance-sheet leverage and credit-guarantee tools to mobilize private capital alongside concessional IDA windows for middle-income and developing nations.

statementBreakdown.reference: IBRD Mandate & World Bank Group Operational Framework
statementBreakdown.explanation: IBRD directly lends to and issues financial guarantees for middle-income and creditworthy low-income governments by raising funds on international capital markets using its AAA credit rating.

IBRD does not work 'single-handedly'—it works alongside its sister World Bank Group arms (especially the International Development Association for the poorest nations, IFC for private enterprise, and MIGA for political risk guarantees) as well as national governments and regional development banks.

statementBreakdown.reference: IBRD Articles of Agreement (1944) — Historical Origin
statementBreakdown.explanation: Created at the 1944 Bretton Woods Conference, IBRD's primary initial mandate was financing the post-World War II reconstruction of war-devastated European economies (its very first loan in 1947 went to France).

visualSuggestion.title: IBRD vs. IDA Within the World Bank Group

rows: Global bond markets backed by AAA rating
Graduated from IDA assistance in 2014 (now an IDA donor)

hook.headline: Does the IBRD work 'single-handedly' to fight poverty in developing countries?
hook.teaser: Notice how that single extreme word in Statement II cracks the entire question in seconds.

keywords.calloutNote: IBRD never works alone—it coordinates closely with IDA (for the poorest countries), IFC (for the private sector), MIGA, and national governments.
activePhrases: single-handedly

keywords.term: loans and guarantees to middle income countries
keywords.calloutTerm: “loans and guarantees to middle income countries”
keywords.calloutNote: While IDA handles concessional aid for the poorest nations, IBRD focuses squarely on lending and guarantees for middle-income economies.
activePhrases: loans and guarantees to middle income countries
dimmedPhrases: single-handedly
contextPhrases: help Europe rebuild after the World War II

verdicts.source: IBRD provides loans, guarantees, and advisory support to middle-income and creditworthy low-income countries.
IBRD does not work single-handedly—it operates alongside IDA, IFC, MIGA, and member governments.
Established at the 1944 Bretton Woods Conference, IBRD's first mission was financing Europe's post-World War II reconstruction.

answer.label: C
answer.text: Knocking out the extreme 'single-handedly' claim leaves IBRD's post-WWII origin and middle-income lending—so I and III only is right.

items.desc: IBRD + IDA form the World Bank; IFC (private sector), MIGA (political risk insurance), and ICSID (disputes) complete the Group.

items.desc: India belongs to IBRD, IDA, IFC, and MIGA, but is not a member of ICSID.

items.desc: Reflecting its 'Reconstruction' title, IBRD issued its very first loan of USD 250 million to France in May 1947.

subject: Economy
stem:
Consider the following statements in respect of RTGS and NEFT :
I. In RTGS, the settlement time is instantaneous while in case of NEFT, it takes some time to settle payments.
II. In RTGS, the customer is charged for inward transactions while that is not the case for NEFT.
III. Operating hours for RTGS are restricted on certain days while this is not true for NEFT.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct ?

keywords.shortNote: A gross settlement system managed by the RBI where funds transfer instructions are processed continuously on a transaction-by-transaction basis in real time without netting.
keywords.concept: Real Time Gross Settlement (RTGS): A gross settlement system managed by the RBI where funds transfer instructions are processed continuously on a transaction-by-transaction basis in real time without netting.

keywords.shortNote: A nationwide retail payment system managed by the RBI that settles fund transfers on a Deferred Net Settlement (DNS) basis in continuous half-hourly batches.
keywords.concept: National Electronic Funds Transfer (NEFT): A nationwide retail payment system managed by the RBI that settles fund transfers on a Deferred Net Settlement (DNS) basis in continuous half-hourly batches.

optionBreakdown.label: a
optionBreakdown.explanation: Only statement I is factually and procedurally accurate. Statements II and III contradict RBI's operational and pricing guidelines.

optionBreakdown.label: b
optionBreakdown.explanation: Customer inward transactions are free across both RTGS and NEFT without exception.

optionBreakdown.label: c
optionBreakdown.explanation: Both RTGS and NEFT operate 24x7x365; there are no day-specific operating window restrictions.

optionBreakdown.label: d
optionBreakdown.explanation: Asserts restricted timing for RTGS, which became obsolete in December 2020.

valueAddition.title: Architectural Distinctions: RTGS vs. NEFT
bullets: Settlement Philosophy: RTGS operates on 'Real Time' (no waiting period) and 'Gross' basis (each transaction settled individually). NEFT operates on Deferred Net Settlement (DNS) where transactions are pooled and netted in 48 half-hourly batches daily.

Transaction Value Limits: RTGS is primarily designed for high-value transactions and mandates a statutory minimum transfer limit of ₹2,00,000 (with no upper ceiling). NEFT has no minimum or maximum limit for account-to-account transfers.
System Ownership: Both payment systems are directly owned, operated, and maintained by the Reserve Bank of India, unlike retail rails like UPI and IMPS which are operated by NPCI.

valueAddition.title: Historical Operational Timelines & Digital Reforms
bullets: Round-the-Clock Rollout: NEFT was made 24x7x365 operational starting December 2019. RTGS followed suit and was made available 24x7x365 on 14 December 2020.

Fee Rationalisation: In July 2019, the RBI waived all processing and service charges levied by it on member banks for RTGS and NEFT, directing banks to pass the benefit to retail customers, completely eliminating inward charges and digital outward retail fees.

inNews.source: Reserve Bank of India / The Hindu
inNews.headline: RBI Enhances High-Value Settlement Resiliency across Continuous 24x7 RTGS and NEFT Core Financial Infrastructure
inNews.relevance: Reaffirms the unbroken 24x7 operational availability of RTGS and NEFT rails, tracking high-value settlement finality and real-time risk mitigation across Indian commercial banking networks.

statementBreakdown.reference: RBI Master Directions on RTGS & NEFT
statementBreakdown.explanation: RTGS settles transactions on a continuous, transaction-by-transaction basis instantaneously without netting. NEFT settles funds on a Deferred Net Settlement (DNS) basis in half-hourly batches across the day, meaning it inherently takes some processing time to clear.

statementBreakdown.reference: RBI Notification on Waiver of Charges (July 2019)
statementBreakdown.explanation: Inward transactions (credits received by the beneficiary customer) are completely free for both RTGS and NEFT. Moreover, RBI mandated that banks cannot levy any processing charges on digital outward NEFT or RTGS initiated online by savings account holders.
Both RTGS and NEFT are operational round the clock—24 hours a day, 7 days a week, 365 days a year—including weekends and public holidays. Neither has restricted operating hours on any day.

visualSuggestion.title: Comprehensive Comparison: RTGS vs. NEFT

rows: Deferred Net Settlement (DNS) in half-hourly batches
Batched (settled at completion of batch window)
No upper ceiling (₹50,000 per transaction for cash-based walk-in)

hook.headline: Does RTGS actually close on weekends?
hook.teaser: Two outdated rules on banking transfers that still trap aspirants in Prelims.

keywords.term: Operating hours for RTGS are restricted
keywords.calloutNote: Outdated rule trap: Both RTGS and NEFT run 24x7x365, with zero downtime on holidays.
activePhrases: Operating hours for RTGS are restricted on certain days while this is not true for NEFT

keywords.term: instantaneous while in case of NEFT, it takes some time
keywords.calloutNote: RTGS is instantaneous gross settlement; NEFT clears in 48 half-hourly batches.
activePhrases: In RTGS, the settlement time is instantaneous while in case of NEFT, it takes some time to settle payments
dimmedPhrases: Operating hours for RTGS are restricted on certain days while this is not true for NEFT
contextPhrases: customer is charged for inward transactions

verdicts.source: RTGS processes each transfer individually in real time, while NEFT bundles transactions into half-hourly batches.
Inward transactions are completely free across all Indian banks for both RTGS and NEFT.
Since December 2020, RTGS operates 24 hours a day, 365 days a year—identical to NEFT.

answer.label: A
answer.text: Only statement I is correct; inward transactions are free on both systems and both operate 24x7x365.

valueAddition.title: Value addition
valueAddition.subtitle: Add these to your Payment Systems notes

items.title: RTGS Floor
items.desc: RTGS is designed for large-value payments with a strict minimum floor of ₹2,00,000.

items.title: NEFT Rhythm
items.desc: Settles continuously every 30 minutes, totaling 48 settlement cycles each calendar day.

items.title: Central Rails
items.desc: Unlike NPCI rails (UPI/IMPS), both RTGS and NEFT are owned and operated by the RBI.

valueAddition.note: Examiners love testing outdated banking rules like physical operating windows and inward charges to penalize candidates relying on stale material.

subject: Economy
stem:
Consider the following countries :
I. United Arab Emirates
II. France
III. Germany
IV. Singapore
V. Bangladesh

How many countries amongst the above are there other than India where international merchant payments are accepted under UPI ?

keywords.shortNote: A wholly-owned subsidiary of the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) incorporated in April 2020 to deploy UPI and RuPay rails globally through cross-border merchant acceptance and P2P remittance linkages.
keywords.concept: NPCI International Payments Limited (NIPL): A wholly-owned subsidiary of the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) incorporated in April 2020 to deploy UPI and RuPay rails globally through cross-border merchant acceptance and P2P remittance linkages.

keywords.shortNote: Enables Indian travelers to scan foreign merchant QR codes using domestic UPI apps (linked to Indian bank accounts) with instant real-time currency conversion debited in Indian Rupees.
keywords.concept: International Merchant Acceptance (P2M): Enables Indian travelers to scan foreign merchant QR codes using domestic UPI apps (linked to Indian bank accounts) with instant real-time currency conversion debited in Indian Rupees.

optionBreakdown.label: a
optionBreakdown.explanation: Under-counts the qualifying countries by omitting one of UAE, France, or Singapore.

optionBreakdown.label: b
optionBreakdown.explanation: Exactly three countries among the list—United Arab Emirates, France, and Singapore—support live international merchant payments under UPI.

optionBreakdown.label: c
optionBreakdown.explanation: Incorrectly assumes either Germany or Bangladesh is live on merchant acceptance.

optionBreakdown.label: d
optionBreakdown.explanation: Falsely presumes all listed diplomatic and trade partners have integrated UPI into domestic retail merchant terminals.

valueAddition.title: NIPL Jurisdictions: Live UPI Merchant Acceptance
bullets: Operational Countries: As recognized by NIPL, international merchant QR acceptance is active in Bhutan, Cambodia, France, Mauritius, Nepal, Qatar, Singapore, Sri Lanka, and the UAE.

Mechanism: An Indian user activates 'UPI International' on their UPI app (PhonePe, Google Pay, BHIM, Paytm), scans the local partner QR code (e.g., NETS in Singapore, Lyra in France, NeoPay in UAE), and the amount is debited directly from their Indian bank account with real-time forex conversion.

Differentiation from P2P Remittance Linkages: Cross-border P2M (merchant shopping) is legally and operationally distinct from bilateral real-time fast-payment interlinks (e.g., UPI–PayNow for personal peer-to-peer family maintenance transfers).

valueAddition.title: UPI International vs. UPI One World
bullets: UPI International: Outbound facility for Indian residents traveling abroad to pay overseas merchants using their domestic UPI-linked bank accounts.

UPI One World: Inbound prepaid payment instrument (PPI) wallet facility provided to foreign nationals and NRIs visiting India from G20 nations and other designated jurisdictions to experience UPI without needing an Indian domestic bank account.

inNews.source: NPCI International Payments Limited / The Hindu
inNews.headline: NIPL Expands Cross-Border QR Code Interoperability and Local Currency Settlement Rails across West Asia and Southeast Asia
inNews.relevance: Directly highlights the strategic international rollout of UPI merchant acceptance, tracking operational integration with local national payment switches.

statementBreakdown.reference: NIPL Partnership with NeoPay (Mashreq) & Network International
statementBreakdown.explanation: UPI person-to-merchant (P2M) payments are live across retail, dining, and tourism spots in the UAE via point-of-sale terminals including Network International, NeoPay, and Magnati.
France became the first European country to accept UPI merchant payments, formally launched at the Eiffel Tower and expanding to major departmental stores (e.g., Galeries Lafayette).
Germany has not rolled out commercial merchant acceptance for UPI. While discussions on cross-border payment integration in Europe continue, no live merchant acquisition rail exists in Germany.
Singapore supports UPI for both bilateral cross-border remittances (UPI-PayNow linkage) and merchant payments by scanning NETS QR codes at participating merchant outlets.
While India and Bangladesh established bilateral trade settlement mechanisms in Indian Rupees (INR) and Bangladeshi Taka (BDT), UPI merchant QR acceptance is not operational in Bangladesh.

hook.headline: In how many foreign countries can you pay via UPI?
hook.teaser: France, Singapore, UAE... but what about Germany? Here is how to nail the exact count.

keywords.term: international merchant payments are accepted under UPI
keywords.calloutNote: Distinguish between active P2M QR merchant acceptance and general bilateral trade currency accords.
activePhrases: international merchant payments are accepted under UPI

keywords.calloutNote: Neither has operationalised UPI merchant QR rails on the ground.
activePhrases: Germany
Bangladesh
dimmedPhrases: international merchant payments are accepted under UPI

verdicts.source: Accepted across UAE retail terminals via partnerships with Network International and Mashreq's NeoPay.
Operational in France via Lyra Network, launched at the Eiffel Tower and luxury retail chains.
Germany has no official live merchant acquisition infrastructure for UPI.
Accepted across Singapore through NETS QR terminals alongside the PayNow remittance linkage.
Bilateral trade uses INR/BDT mechanisms, but retail UPI merchant payments are not available.

answer.label: B
answer.text: Only three countries—the UAE, France, and Singapore—support live international merchant payments under UPI.

subject: Economy
stem:
Consider the following statements about 'PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana' :
I. It targets installation of one crore solar rooftop panels in the residential sector.
II. The Ministry of New and Renewable Energy aims to impart training on installation, operation, maintenance and repairs of solar rooftop systems at grassroot levels.
III. It aims to create more than three lakhs skilled manpower through fresh skilling, and up-skilling, under scheme component of capacity building.

Which of the statements given above are correct ?

keywords.term: PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana
keywords.shortNote: A flagship Central Sector Scheme launched in February 2024 with an outlay of Rs. 75,021 crore to equip one crore residential households with subsidized rooftop solar installations and up to 300 units of free electricity per month.
keywords.concept: PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana: A flagship Central Sector Scheme launched in February 2024 with an outlay of Rs. 75,021 crore to equip one crore residential households with subsidized rooftop solar installations and up to 300 units of free electricity per month.

keywords.shortNote: Direct upfront capital subsidy credited to residential consumers' bank accounts upon commissioning of grid-connected rooftop solar plants—set at Rs. 30,000 for 1 kW, Rs. 60,000 for 2 kW, and capped at Rs. 78,000 for 3 kW or above.
keywords.concept: Central Financial Assistance (CFA): Direct upfront capital subsidy credited to residential consumers' bank accounts upon commissioning of grid-connected rooftop solar plants—set at Rs. 30,000 for 1 kW, Rs. 60,000 for 2 kW, and capped at Rs. 78,000 for 3 kW or above.

keywords.shortNote: A billing mechanism allowing rooftop solar owners to export surplus solar electricity to the local DISCOM grid and receive credits against electricity drawn during non-solar hours.
keywords.concept: Net Metering: A billing mechanism allowing rooftop solar owners to export surplus solar electricity to the local DISCOM grid and receive credits against electricity drawn during non-solar hours.

optionBreakdown.label: a
optionBreakdown.explanation: Misses the explicit three-lakh skilled manpower target documented in MNRE's capacity-building guidelines.

optionBreakdown.label: b
optionBreakdown.explanation: Overlooks the grassroot training mandate for installation, operation, maintenance, and repairs.

optionBreakdown.label: c
optionBreakdown.explanation: Excludes the headline goal of one crore residential solar rooftops.

optionBreakdown.label: d
optionBreakdown.explanation: All three statements lift exact targets and operational components verbatim from MNRE's official scheme release.

valueAddition.title: Subsidy Slabs & Institutional Architecture
bullets: Total Outlay & Tenure: Rs. 75,021 crore Central Sector Scheme implemented through FY 2026–27 via the National Portal (pmsuryaghar.gov.in) with REC Limited acting as the National Programme Implementation Agency (NPIA).
CFA Subsidy Structure: Rs. 30,000 for 1 kW, Rs. 60,000 for 2 kW, and Rs. 78,000 for 3 kW or higher capacity—covering roughly 60% of system cost for 2 kW plants and 40% for 2–3 kW increments.
Model Solar Village: One village per district is developed as a Model Solar Village with a Rs. 1 crore grant to demonstrate 100% solarized rural self-reliance.

valueAddition.title: Economic & Fiscal Rationale
bullets: Eliminates domestic electricity bills for lower- and middle-income households while letting prosumers sell surplus daytime solar power back to DISCOMs.
Lowers peak daytime thermal power demand, eases DISCOM cross-subsidy burdens, and builds a decentralized green-collar workforce across rural and semi-urban India.

inNews.source: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE) / PIB
inNews.headline: PM Surya Ghar Crosses 45 Lakh Rooftop Installations as DISCOM Incentives Accelerate
inNews.relevance: MNRE reported in October 2026 that residential rooftop solar installations under PM Surya Ghar surpassed 45 lakh households, aided by streamlined vendor empanelment and DISCOM performance incentives.

statementBreakdown.explanation: Approved in February 2024, the scheme explicitly targets installing rooftop solar systems across one crore residential households nationwide, providing up to 300 units of free electricity monthly.
Under the scheme's capacity-building pillar, MNRE conducts grassroot-level technical training covering installation, operation, preventive maintenance, and repair of rooftop solar systems.

statementBreakdown.reference: PIB / MNRE Official Release — Skilling Target
statementBreakdown.explanation: The capacity-building component targets creating over three lakh skilled personnel—including at least one lakh Solar Mitras—through fresh skilling and upskilling programs.

rows: Up to 300 units of free electricity per month via net metering
Fresh skilling & upskilling in installation, O&M, and repairs
Central Sector Scheme; REC Limited as National Implementation Agency

hook.teaser: Notice how UPSC lifts all three statements straight from MNRE's official scheme release without a single trap.

subject: Economy
stem:
Consider the following statements with regard to BRICS :
I. 16th BRICS Summit was held under the Chairship of Russia in Kazan.
II. Indonesia has become a full member of BRICS.
III. The theme of the 16th BRICS Summit was Strengthening Multiculturalism for Just Global Development and Security.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct ?

keywords.shortNote: The annual summit of BRICS leaders hosted by Russia in Kazan from October 22–24, 2024 under the official theme 'Strengthening Multilateralism for Just Global Development and Security', adopting the Kazan Declaration and launching the BRICS Partner Country category.
keywords.concept: 16th BRICS Summit (Kazan, October 2024): The annual summit of BRICS leaders hosted by Russia in Kazan from October 22–24, 2024 under the official theme 'Strengthening Multilateralism for Just Global Development and Security', adopting the Kazan Declaration and launching the BRICS Partner Country category.

keywords.shortNote: The enlargement of the original five-member bloc (Brazil, Russia, India, China, South Africa) through the admission of Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, and the United Arab Emirates in January 2024, followed by Indonesia joining as a full member in January 2025.
keywords.concept: BRICS Expansion (BRICS+): The enlargement of the original five-member bloc (Brazil, Russia, India, China, South Africa) through the admission of Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, and the United Arab Emirates in January 2024, followed by Indonesia joining as a full member in January 2025.

keywords.shortNote: Multilateralism refers to coordinated diplomatic, economic, and institutional cooperation among multiple nations within global governance frameworks, whereas multiculturalism denotes cultural diversity within a society—a deliberate single-word substitution used in Statement III.
keywords.concept: Multilateralism vs. Multiculturalism: Multilateralism refers to coordinated diplomatic, economic, and institutional cooperation among multiple nations within global governance frameworks, whereas multiculturalism denotes cultural diversity within a society—a deliberate single-word substitution used in Statement III.

optionBreakdown.label: a
optionBreakdown.explanation: Accurately confirms Russia's Kazan Chairship for the 16th Summit and Indonesia's full membership admission in January 2025 while catching the 'Multiculturalism' word swap in Statement III.

optionBreakdown.label: b

valueAddition.title: Current BRICS Full-Member Roster & Partner-Country Framework
bullets: Founding Five (BRICS): Brazil, Russia, India, China, and South Africa (joined 2010).

2024–2025 Full Members: Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, and the United Arab Emirates joined effective January 1, 2024 (while Saudi Arabia delayed formal completion and Argentina declined), and Indonesia became the tenth full member in January 2025.

BRICS Partner Country Category (Kazan 2024): At the 16th Kazan Summit, leaders created a new 'Partner Country' tier (inviting nations such as Belarus, Bolivia, Cuba, Kazakhstan, Malaysia, Nigeria, Thailand, Uganda, and Uzbekistan) to deepen economic cooperation without immediate full-member expansion.

valueAddition.title: Key Economic & Financial Initiatives of BRICS
bullets: New Development Bank (NDB): Headquartered in Shanghai and established via the 2014 Fortaleza Declaration to mobilize infrastructure and sustainable development finance for emerging economies.

Contingent Reserve Arrangement (CRA): A USD 100 billion liquidity pool designed to shield member nations against short-term Balance of Payments pressures, complemented at Kazan by work on cross-border local-currency payment mechanisms and BRICS Clear.
