subject: Indian Polity
stem:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Parliament of India can place a particular law in the Ninth Schedule of the Constitution of India.
2. The validity of a law placed in the Ninth Schedule cannot be examined by any court and no judgement can be made on it.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

keywords.shortNote: A constitutional repository created by Article 31B via the 1st Amendment Act, 1951, to accord statutory immunity against Part III challenges.
keywords.concept: Ninth Schedule: A constitutional repository created by Article 31B via the 1st Amendment Act, 1951, to accord statutory immunity against Part III challenges.

keywords.shortNote: Constitutional validating device saving Acts and Regulations specified in the Ninth Schedule from voidness on grounds of inconsistency with Fundamental Rights.
keywords.concept: Article 31B: Constitutional validating device saving Acts and Regulations specified in the Ninth Schedule from voidness on grounds of inconsistency with Fundamental Rights.

keywords.shortNote: Constitutional authority of the Supreme Court and High Courts to examine the legislative and executive actions against constitutional mandates.
keywords.concept: Judicial Review: Constitutional authority of the Supreme Court and High Courts to examine the legislative and executive actions against constitutional mandates.

keywords.shortNote: Judicial principle enunciated in Kesavananda Bharati (1973) limiting Parliament's amending power under Article 368 from altering core constitutional tenets.
keywords.concept: Basic Structure Doctrine: Judicial principle enunciated in Kesavananda Bharati (1973) limiting Parliament's amending power under Article 368 from altering core constitutional tenets.

optionBreakdown.label: a
optionBreakdown.explanation: Option (a) is correct because Statement 1 represents an authentic constitutional power while Statement 2 is invalidated by the I.R. Coelho ruling.

valueAddition.title: The I.R. Coelho Doctrine & The 24 April 1973 Cut-Off
bullets: Kesavananda Cut-Off Line: The 9-judge bench in I.R. Coelho (2007) drew a decisive temporal boundary at 24 April 1973 (the date of the Kesavananda Bharati verdict).

Dual Test of Validity: A post-1973 Ninth Schedule law must satisfy both the 'Rights Test' (infringement of Articles 14, 19, or 21) and the 'Essence of the Rights Test' (whether the violation damages the Basic Structure).

Judicial Review as Basic Structure: Reaffirmed that judicial review is an integral component of the Basic Structure (established in Minerva Mills and L. Chandra Kumar) and cannot be excluded via Article 31B.

valueAddition.title: Common Exam Trap: Textual Immunity vs. Judicial Reality
bullets: Bare Text vs Case Law: Article 31B's literal text states 'none of the Acts and Regulations... shall be deemed to be void', making candidates believe immunity is absolute if they only read the bare article.

Extreme Absolute Words: Statement 2 uses 'cannot be examined by any court and no judgement can be made'—such categorical exclusions in Polity questions are classic red flags that almost always indicate an incorrect statement.
Pre-1973 vs Post-1973 Shield: Pre-1973 insertions remain immune from judicial scrutiny; only post-1973 laws are subject to the Basic Structure test.

Consider the following statements:
1. The Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 replaced the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954.
2. The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) is under the charge of Director General of Health Services in the Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

keywords.shortNote: An omnibus consolidation statute enacted to harmonize multiple disparate food control orders and acts under a single scientific regulatory umbrella.
keywords.concept: Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006: An omnibus consolidation statute enacted to harmonize multiple disparate food control orders and acts under a single scientific regulatory umbrella.

keywords.shortNote: Section 5 of the FSS Act establishes an independent Chairperson (rank of Secretary to the Government of India) and a Chief Executive Officer (rank of Additional Secretary), not the DGHS.
keywords.concept: FSSAI Structure: Section 5 of the FSS Act establishes an independent Chairperson (rank of Secretary to the Government of India) and a Chief Executive Officer (rank of Additional Secretary), not the DGHS.

optionBreakdown.label: a
optionBreakdown.explanation: Statement 1 is historically and legally accurate; statement 2 falsely places FSSAI under the Director General of Health Services.

optionBreakdown.label: b
optionBreakdown.explanation: FSSAI is an autonomous statutory authority headed by a Chairperson and CEO, not the DGHS.

optionBreakdown.label: c
optionBreakdown.explanation: Statement 2 confuses an attached technical directorate (DGHS) with an independent statutory authority.

optionBreakdown.label: d
optionBreakdown.explanation: Statement 1 correctly describes the repeal and replacement of the 1954 Act by the 2006 Act.

valueAddition.title: Legislative Consolidation under FSS Act, 2006
bullets: Integrated 8 Pre-existing Statutes/Orders: Repealed the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954; Fruit Products Order, 1955; Meat Food Products Order, 1973; Vegetable Oil Products (Control) Order, 1947; Edible Oils Packaging (Regulation) Order, 1998; Solvent Extracted Oil, De-oiled Meal and Edible Flour (Control) Order, 1967; Milk and Milk Products Order, 1992; and provisions under the Essential Commodities Act, 1955 relating to food.
Shift in Regulatory Paradigm: Shifted from multi-departmental policing of adulteration to a single science-based standard-setting and risk-assessment regime from farm to fork.

valueAddition.title: Institutional Architecture of FSSAI
bullets: Administrative Ministry: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (MoHFW) serves as the nodal administrative ministry.
Composition (Section 5): Consists of a Chairperson and 22 members, out of which one-third (at least 7) must be women.
Executive Head (Section 7): Chief Executive Officer (CEO), appointed by the Central Government not below the rank of Additional Secretary to GoI, who functions as Member-Secretary to the Authority.
Scientific Committees & Panels: Formulates mandatory standards via independent Scientific Panels and a Central Scientific Committee comprising domain researchers.

subject: Indian Polity
stem:
With reference to the election of the President of India, consider the following statements:
1. The value of the vote of each MLA varies from State to State.
2. The value of the vote of MPs of the Lok Sabha is more than the value of the vote of MPs of the Rajya Sabha.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

keywords.shortNote: Determines the value of an MLA's vote by dividing the State's 1971 population by total elected assembly seats multiplied by 1,000.
keywords.concept: Article 55(2)(a): Determines the value of an MLA's vote by dividing the State's 1971 population by total elected assembly seats multiplied by 1,000.

keywords.shortNote: Determines uniform vote values for all elected MPs by dividing the cumulative vote value of all MLAs nationwide by total elected MPs of both Houses.
keywords.concept: Article 55(2)(c): Determines uniform vote values for all elected MPs by dividing the cumulative vote value of all MLAs nationwide by total elected MPs of both Houses.

optionBreakdown.label: a
optionBreakdown.explanation: Identifies Statement 1 as the sole correct statement.

valueAddition.title: Article 55: Parity Principles & Formulas
bullets: Inter-State Parity: Achieved by pegging MLA vote value to state population per elected seat based on the 1971 Census.
Union-State Parity: Total vote value of all elected MPs across Parliament equals the aggregate vote value of all elected MLAs across India.
MP Vote Formula: $\text{Value of 1 MP Vote} = \frac{\text{Total value of votes of all elected MLAs of all States}}{\text{Total number of elected members of both Houses of Parliament}}$.
Equal MP Weights: Every elected MP—Lok Sabha or Rajya Sabha—casts a vote of identical mathematical value.

valueAddition.title: Presidential Electoral College Composition
bullets: Included: Elected MPs of Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha; elected MLAs of all States, NCT of Delhi, and UT of Puducherry.
Excluded: Nominated members of Parliament; nominated MLAs; all members of State Legislative Councils (Vidhan Parishad).

inNews.relevance: Directly highlights the parity mechanisms and vote value formulas under Article 55.

Consider the following statements in respect of election to the President of India:
1. The members nominated to either House of the Parliament or the Legislative Assemblies of States are also eligible to be included in the Electoral College.
2. Higher the number of elective Assembly seats, higher is the value of vote of each MLA of that State.
3. The value of vote of each MLA of Madhya Pradesh is greater than that of Kerala.
4. The value of vote of each MLA of Puducherry is higher than that of Arunachal Pradesh...
How many of the above statements are correct?
(a) Only one
(b) Only two
(c) Only three
(d) All four

statementBreakdown.explanation: Because populations and elective assembly seats differ across States, the value of an MLA's vote varies from State to State (ranging from 7 in Sikkim to 208 in Uttar Pradesh).
Under Article 55(2)(c), the value of vote of every elected MP is identical regardless of whether they belong to the Lok Sabha or the Rajya Sabha (700 in the 2022 Presidential Election).

optionBreakdown.reference: Job Reservation · Not an RPL Objective
optionBreakdown.explanation: RPL provides competency assessment, accidental insurance, and formal skill certification to improve employability and wages—it does not create job reservations in Public Sector Undertakings.

optionBreakdown.reference: Short-Term Training (STT) vs. Prior Informal Learning

valueAddition.title: How Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) Works on the Ground
bullets: Target Group & Zero-Fee Assessment: Over 90% of India's workforce operates in the informal sector with skills learned on construction sites, workshops, or family trades; RPL conducts a 12-to-80 hour orientation and practical assessment free of cost to issue an NSQF-aligned certificate.

Tangible Benefits to Workers: Certified workers gain formal proof of competence for domestic and overseas jobs (such as Gulf construction corridors), access to bank credit under MUDRA, and 3-year accidental insurance coverage under Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana (PMSBY).

subject: Economy
stem: Which of the following gives 'Global Gender Gap Index' ranking to the countries of the world?

keywords.shortNote: An annual benchmark published since 2006 assessing progress toward gender parity across economic, educational, health, and political dimensions on a scale from 0 to 1.
keywords.concept: Global Gender Gap Index: An annual benchmark published since 2006 assessing progress toward gender parity across economic, educational, health, and political dimensions on a scale from 0 to 1.

keywords.shortNote: An independent international non-governmental organization based in Cologny, Geneva, renowned for flagship benchmarking reports such as the Global Competitiveness Report and Global Risks Report.
keywords.concept: World Economic Forum (WEF): An independent international non-governmental organization based in Cologny, Geneva, renowned for flagship benchmarking reports such as the Global Competitiveness Report and Global Risks Report.

optionBreakdown.label: a
optionBreakdown.explanation: The World Economic Forum compiles and publishes the Global Gender Gap Index annually to quantify the magnitude of gender disparities across four key sub-indices.

optionBreakdown.label: b
optionBreakdown.explanation: UNHRC is an intergovernmental body within the United Nations system responsible for promoting and protecting human rights globally, notably via the Universal Periodic Review, but does not publish this index.

optionBreakdown.label: c
optionBreakdown.explanation: UN Women is the United Nations entity dedicated to gender equality and women's empowerment; it issues reports like 'Progress on the Sustainable Development Goals: The Gender Snapshot', but not the Global Gender Gap Index.

optionBreakdown.label: d
optionBreakdown.explanation: WHO focuses on global public health indicators and releases reports such as the World Health Statistics Report, rather than composite cross-sector gender gap rankings.

valueAddition.title: Architecture of the Global Gender Gap Index
bullets: Four Sub-Indices: 1) Economic Participation and Opportunity (labour force participation, wage equality, technical/professional workers), 2) Educational Attainment (literacy rate, primary, secondary, and tertiary enrolment), 3) Health and Survival (sex ratio at birth, healthy life expectancy), 4) Political Empowerment (women in parliament, ministerial positions, years as head of state).
Focus on Parity, Not Levels: Evaluates the gap between women and men within each country irrespective of that nation's absolute level of economic development or resources.
Scoring Scale: Ranges from 0 (complete inequality/imparity) to 1 (complete equality/full parity).

valueAddition.title: Flagship Reports Published by the World Economic Forum

Global Risks Report (annual evaluation of systemic economic, environmental, and geopolitical hazards)
Energy Transition Index (Fostering Effective Energy Transition)
Future of Jobs Report (tracking workforce transformations and technological disruption)
Travel & Tourism Development Index (TTDI)

valueAddition.title: Related Gender Indices by Other International Bodies
bullets: Gender Inequality Index (GII) & Gender Development Index (GDI): Published by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) in its Human Development Report.
Gender Social Norms Index (GSNI): Published by UNDP to evaluate societal biases and prejudices against women.
Women, Business and the Law Index: Published annually by the World Bank assessing structural and legal barriers across a woman's working lifetime.

subject: Economy
stem:
What is/are the most likely advantages of implementing 'Goods and Services Tax (GST)'?
1. It will replace multiple taxes collected by multiple authorities and will thus create a single market in India.
2. It will drastically reduce the 'Current Account Deficit' of India and will enable it to increase its foreign exchange reserves.
3. It will enormously increase the growth and size of economy of India and will enable it to overtake China in the near future.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:

keywords.shortNote: A comprehensive, multi-stage, destination-based indirect tax introduced via the 101st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2016 (effective July 1, 2017) that subsumed major Central and State indirect taxes into a unified national market.
keywords.concept: Goods and Services Tax (GST): A comprehensive, multi-stage, destination-based indirect tax introduced via the 101st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2016 (effective July 1, 2017) that subsumed major Central and State indirect taxes into a unified national market.

keywords.shortNote: The tax-on-tax distortion in pre-GST indirect taxation where non-creditable levies at successive stages of production and inter-state trade inflated final consumer prices.
keywords.concept: Cascading Effect of Taxes: The tax-on-tax distortion in pre-GST indirect taxation where non-creditable levies at successive stages of production and inter-state trade inflated final consumer prices.

keywords.shortNote: The seamless tax-offset mechanism under GST allowing businesses to deduct GST paid on inputs and input services from the GST payable on final output across the entire value chain.
keywords.concept: Input Tax Credit (ITC): The seamless tax-offset mechanism under GST allowing businesses to deduct GST paid on inputs and input services from the GST payable on final output across the entire value chain.

keywords.shortNote: The taxation principle under which GST revenue accrues to the State where goods or services are finally consumed rather than the State where they are manufactured.
keywords.concept: Destination-Based Taxation: The taxation principle under which GST revenue accrues to the State where goods or services are finally consumed rather than the State where they are manufactured.

optionBreakdown.label: a
optionBreakdown.explanation: Accurately captures the core structural purpose of GST—eliminating tax fragmentation across Centre and States to build a single national market—while rejecting exaggerated macroeconomic claims.

optionBreakdown.label: b
optionBreakdown.explanation: Relies entirely on two hyperbolic assertions about Current Account Deficit and overtaking China.

optionBreakdown.label: c
optionBreakdown.explanation: Accepts the unrealistic claim that GST alone enables India to overtake China's economy in the near future.

optionBreakdown.label: d
optionBreakdown.explanation: Fails to filter out extreme modifiers ('drastically', 'enormously', 'overtake China in the near future').

valueAddition.title: What GST Subsumed vs. What Remains Outside GST
bullets: Subsumed Central Taxes: Central Excise Duty, Additional Duties of Excise, Service Tax, Countervailing Duty (CVD), and Special Additional Duty of Customs (SAD).
Subsumed State Taxes: State VAT/Sales Tax, Central Sales Tax (CST), Luxury Tax, Entry Tax/Octroi, Entertainment Tax (except those levied by local bodies), and Taxes on lotteries/betting.

Kept Outside GST: Alcohol for human consumption (permanently excluded under Article 366(12A)), five petroleum products (crude oil, petrol, diesel, ATF, natural gas—until GST Council notifies a date), Basic Customs Duty, and Stamp Duty.

valueAddition.title: Institutional Design: GST Council (Article 279A)
bullets: Chaired by the Union Finance Minister with the Union Minister of State (Revenue) and State Finance/Taxation Ministers as members.

Every decision requires a three-fourths (75%) majority of weighted votes cast—where the Central Government carries one-third (33.33%) weight and all State Governments together carry two-thirds (66.67%) weight, ensuring neither Centre nor States can act unilaterally.

inNews.source: Ministry of Finance / GST Council
inNews.headline: Gross Monthly GST Collections Cross Rs. 1.87 Lakh Crore in October 2026 on Festive Consumption and Compliance
inNews.relevance: October 2026 GST revenue figures reinforced steady domestic formalization and Input Tax Credit matching, while the GST Council continued deliberations on rate rationalization and inverted duty structure corrections.

statementBreakdown.reference: Constitution (101st Amendment) Act, 2016 — One Nation, One Tax
statementBreakdown.explanation: GST subsumed 17 Central and State indirect taxes (such as Central Excise, Service Tax, State VAT, CST, Entry Tax, and Octroi) and dismantled inter-state check-posts, unifying India into a single common market.

statementBreakdown.reference: External Sector & Balance of Payments Dynamics
statementBreakdown.explanation: GST is a domestic indirect tax reform; while zero-rating exports improves marginal export competitiveness, GST does not 'drastically reduce' India's Current Account Deficit (which is driven primarily by crude oil, gold, and electronics imports) or directly build forex reserves.

While GST improves formalization and logistics efficiency (estimated to add roughly 0.5–1.5% to medium-term GDP growth), claiming it will 'enormously' expand India's economy to 'overtake China in the near future' (whose GDP is several times larger) is an exaggerated distractor.

State Excise on Alcohol, VAT on Petroleum, Stamp Duty, Electricity Duty

States collectively hold 2/3rd voting weight; 75% majority required

hook.headline: Will GST help India overtake China's economy in the near future?
hook.teaser: Notice how extreme words like 'drastically' and 'enormously' hand you the answer without complex math.

keywords.calloutTerm: “replace multiple taxes collected by multiple authorities”
keywords.calloutNote: That is the exact core mission of GST—merging 17 Central and State indirect taxes into One Nation, One Tax.

GST is a domestic indirect tax—it cannot drastically cut India's Current Account Deficit or directly build forex reserves.
GST adds efficiency to GDP growth, but claiming it will enormously expand India's economy to overtake China soon is completely unrealistic.

answer.label: A
answer.text: Knocking out the two exaggerated claims in Statements 2 and 3 leaves 1 only as the clean answer.

items.desc: Alcohol for human consumption is permanently outside GST; crude oil, petrol, diesel, ATF, and natural gas await Council notification.

subject: Economy
stem:
Consider the following statements:
1. Tax revenue as a percent of GDP of India has steadily increased in the last decade.
2. Fiscal deficit as a percent of GDP of India has steadily increased in the last decade.
Which of the statements given above is/are corrects

keywords.shortNote: Total tax collections of the government expressed as a percentage of nominal Gross Domestic Product, measuring a state's capacity to mobilize tax resources in proportion to economic output.
keywords.concept: Tax-to-GDP Ratio: Total tax collections of the government expressed as a percentage of nominal Gross Domestic Product, measuring a state's capacity to mobilize tax resources in proportion to economic output.

keywords.shortNote: The government's net annual borrowing requirement expressed as a percentage of nominal GDP, serving as the primary benchmark for fiscal sustainability and FRBM compliance.
keywords.concept: Fiscal Deficit-to-GDP Ratio: The government's net annual borrowing requirement expressed as a percentage of nominal GDP, serving as the primary benchmark for fiscal sustainability and FRBM compliance.

keywords.shortNote: The responsiveness of tax revenue growth to changes in nominal GDP, calculated as the percentage change in tax collections divided by the percentage change in nominal GDP.
keywords.concept: Tax Buoyancy: The responsiveness of tax revenue growth to changes in nominal GDP, calculated as the percentage change in tax collections divided by the percentage change in nominal GDP.

optionBreakdown.label: a
optionBreakdown.explanation: Overlooks the post-2008 dip and multi-year stagnation in India's tax-to-GDP ratio.

optionBreakdown.label: b
optionBreakdown.explanation: Ignores the sustained fiscal consolidation glide path between FY 2009–10 (6.5%) and FY 2016–17 (3.5%).

optionBreakdown.label: c
optionBreakdown.explanation: Fails to catch the absolute modifier 'steadily increased', which rarely holds across a ten-year macroeconomic cycle.

optionBreakdown.label: d
optionBreakdown.explanation: Both ratios experienced sharp reversals across the 2008 Global Financial Crisis and subsequent consolidation—neither increased steadily.

valueAddition.title: Why Macroeconomic Ratios Never Move 'Steadily' Over a Decade
bullets: Over any ten-year window in an open emerging economy, business cycles, global shocks (such as the 2008 Global Financial Crisis or the 2020 COVID-19 pandemic), and discretionary fiscal stimulus cause sharp swings in both tax collections and deficits.

Between FY 2007–08 and FY 2016–17, Central Gross Tax-to-GDP fell from 11.9% to 9.6% (FY10) before recovering to ~11.2% (FY17), while Central Fiscal Deficit spiked from 2.5% to 6.5% (FY10) before falling every year down to 3.5% (FY17).

valueAddition.title: Post-2020 Parallel Trajectory for Current Prelims
bullets: The exact same cyclical pattern repeated in the 2020s: Central Fiscal Deficit jumped to 9.2% of GDP in FY 2020–21 during COVID-19, then consolidated steadily down to 4.8% in FY 2024–25 and below 4.5% in FY 2025–26.
Gross Central Tax-to-GDP rose above 11.6% by FY 2024–26, driven by formalization under GST and higher direct tax buoyancy.

inNews.source: Ministry of Finance / RBI Bulletin
inNews.headline: Centre's Gross Tax-to-GDP Ratio Holds Above 11.7% in FY27 as Direct Taxes Outpace Nominal GDP
inNews.relevance: Union Finance Ministry fiscal data reviewed in October 2026 confirmed that sustained direct tax buoyancy kept gross tax-to-GDP near multi-decade highs while the fiscal deficit remained on its downward consolidation path.

statementBreakdown.reference: Economic Survey — Gross Tax Revenue Trends (2007–2017)
statementBreakdown.explanation: India's gross central tax-to-GDP ratio did not rise steadily over the decade; it peaked around 11.9% in FY 2007–08, dropped sharply to ~9.6% after the 2008 Global Financial Crisis stimulus tax cuts, and fluctuated around 10–11% thereafter.

India's central fiscal deficit-to-GDP ratio moved cyclically rather than steadily upward—spiking from 2.5% in FY 2007–08 to 6.5% in FY 2009–10 due to crisis stimulus, and then steadily declining down to 3.5% by FY 2016–17.

visualSuggestion.title: Decadal Swings in India's Key Fiscal Ratios (2007–2017 & 2020–2026)

rows: Consolidated down to 3.5% of GDP (Not steady)

hook.headline: Have India's tax-to-GDP and fiscal deficit ever 'steadily increased' for ten straight years?
hook.teaser: Notice how one single word—steadily—gives away the trap in both statements.

keywords.term: steadily increased in the last decade
keywords.calloutNote: In macroeconomics, 'steadily increased' means rising every single year without a dip—impossible across a decade containing the 2008 Global Financial Crisis.
activePhrases: steadily increased in the last decade

keywords.term: Fiscal deficit as a percent of GDP
keywords.calloutTerm: “Fiscal deficit as a percent of GDP”
keywords.calloutNote: India's fiscal deficit spiked to 6.5% after the 2008 crisis and then fell every year down to 3.5% by 2016–17—the exact opposite of a steady rise.
activePhrases: Fiscal deficit as a percent of GDP
dimmedPhrases: steadily increased in the last decade
contextPhrases: Tax revenue as a percent of GDP

verdicts.source: India's tax-to-GDP ratio fell from 11.9% in 2007–08 to 9.6% after the 2008 financial crisis before recovering, so it never rose steadily.
After spiking to 6.5% in 2009–10, India's fiscal deficit-to-GDP ratio steadily decreased down to 3.5% by 2016–17.

answer.label: D
answer.text: Both ratios swung sharply across the 2008 crisis and recovery—neither increased steadily, so Neither 1 nor 2 is right.

valueAddition.subtitle: Add these to your Budget & Economy Trend notes

items.title: Recent Consolidation Path
items.desc: Central fiscal deficit peaked at 9.2% in FY21 and declined steadily toward the FRBM sub-4.5% target by FY26.

subject: Economy
stem:
With reference to the 'National Intellectual Property Rights Policy, consider the following statements:
1. It reiterates India's commitment to the Doha Development Agenda and the TRIPS Agreement.
2. Department of Industrial Policy and Promotion is the nodal agency for regulating intellectual property rights in India.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?

keywords.shortNote: India's first comprehensive IPR framework approved in May 2016 under the tagline 'Creative India; Innovative India', uniting all IP laws and administration under a single institutional umbrella.
keywords.concept: National Intellectual Property Rights (IPR) Policy, 2016: India's first comprehensive IPR framework approved in May 2016 under the tagline 'Creative India; Innovative India', uniting all IP laws and administration under a single institutional umbrella.

keywords.shortNote: The WTO trade negotiation round launched in November 2001 that affirmed TRIPS flexibilities—such as compulsory licensing—to protect public health and access to affordable medicines.
keywords.concept: Doha Development Agenda (2001): The WTO trade negotiation round launched in November 2001 that affirmed TRIPS flexibilities—such as compulsory licensing—to protect public health and access to affordable medicines.

keywords.term: Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT)
keywords.shortNote: The Ministry of Commerce and Industry department (formerly DIPP) designated as the nodal agency for coordinating, guiding, and overseeing IPR implementation in India.
keywords.concept: Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT): The Ministry of Commerce and Industry department (formerly DIPP) designated as the nodal agency for coordinating, guiding, and overseeing IPR implementation in India.

optionBreakdown.label: a
optionBreakdown.explanation: Eliminated because Statement 2 is also true.

optionBreakdown.label: b
optionBreakdown.explanation: Eliminated because Statement 1 is also true.

optionBreakdown.label: c
optionBreakdown.explanation: The 2016 National IPR Policy unified IP administration under DIPP (now DPIIT) while affirming India's commitment to TRIPS and Doha public-health flexibilities.

optionBreakdown.label: d
optionBreakdown.explanation: Eliminated because both statements are drawn directly from the core mandate of the National IPR Policy.

valueAddition.title: Architecture of the National IPR Policy (2016)
bullets: Tagline & Seven Objectives: Guided by 'Creative India; Innovative India', the policy rests on seven pillars—IPR Awareness, Generation of IPRs, Legal & Legislative Framework, Administration & Management, Commercialization, Enforcement & Adjudication, and Human Capital Development.

Institutional Consolidation: Prior to 2016, Copyright was handled by the Ministry of Human Resource Development and Semiconductor Layout-Design by MeitY; the policy consolidated administration under DIPP (now DPIIT) and established the Cell for IPR Promotion and Management (CIPAM).

valueAddition.title: Why Doha Development Agenda Matters to India
bullets: The 2001 Doha Declaration on the TRIPS Agreement and Public Health confirmed that intellectual property rules should not prevent members from protecting public health.
It backs India's statutory safeguards under the Patents Act—specifically Section 3(d) preventing patent evergreening and Section 84 enabling compulsory licensing for affordable generic medicines.

subject: Economy
stem:
With reference to the 'Prohibition of Benami Property Transactions Act, 1988 (PBPT Act)', consider the following statements:
1. A property transaction is not treated as a benami transaction if the owner of the property is not aware of the transaction.
2. Properties held benami are liable for confiscation by the Government.
3. The Act provides for three authorities for investigations but does not provide for any appellate mechanism.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

keywords.shortNote: A transaction or arrangement where a property is transferred to or held by one person while the consideration has been paid by another person for their immediate or future benefit—explicitly expanded in 2016 to include transactions in a fictitious name, where the owner denies knowledge of ownership, or where the person providing consideration is untraceable.
keywords.concept: Benami Transaction (Section 2(9)): A transaction or arrangement where a property is transferred to or held by one person while the consideration has been paid by another person for their immediate or future benefit—explicitly expanded in 2016 to include transactions in a fictitious name, where the owner denies knowledge of ownership, or where the person providing consideration is untraceable.

keywords.shortNote: The statutory power enabling the Central Government to confiscate any property held benami once adjudicated as benami, without paying any compensation to the benamidar or beneficial owner.
keywords.concept: Confiscation of Benami Property (Section 5 & Section 27): The statutory power enabling the Central Government to confiscate any property held benami once adjudicated as benami, without paying any compensation to the benamidar or beneficial owner.

keywords.shortNote: The enforcement architecture established under the 2016 Amendment comprising four authorities—Initiating Officer, Approving Authority, Administrator, and Adjudicating Authority—backed by a dedicated Appellate Tribunal (Section 30) and appeal to the High Court (Section 49).
keywords.concept: Four-Tier Institutional & Appellate Hierarchy: The enforcement architecture established under the 2016 Amendment comprising four authorities—Initiating Officer, Approving Authority, Administrator, and Adjudicating Authority—backed by a dedicated Appellate Tribunal (Section 30) and appeal to the High Court (Section 49).

optionBreakdown.label: a
optionBreakdown.explanation: Reverses Section 2(9)(A)(c): an ostensible owner's ignorance or denial of ownership is itself a hallmark of a benami transaction.

optionBreakdown.label: b
optionBreakdown.explanation: Accurately identifies confiscation by the Government as the core civil consequence while rejecting the inverted definition in Statement 1 and the false 'no appellate mechanism' claim in Statement 3.

optionBreakdown.label: c
optionBreakdown.explanation: Accepts two false statutory claims while omitting the central confiscation provision.

optionBreakdown.label: d
optionBreakdown.explanation: Overlooks the statutory Appellate Tribunal (Section 30) and High Court appeal remedy (Section 49).

valueAddition.title: Four Expanded Categories of Benami Transactions (2016 Amendment)
bullets: 1. Classic Benami: Property held by one person (benamidar) while consideration is paid by another (beneficial owner) for their immediate or future benefit.
2. Fictitious Name: Transaction or arrangement carried out in a fictitious or non-existent person's name.
3. Owner Unaware / Denies Knowledge: Where the ostensible owner of the property is not aware of or denies knowledge of such ownership (directly refuting Statement 1).
4. Untraceable Payer: Where the person providing the consideration for the property is not traceable or is fictitious.

valueAddition.title: Statutory Exceptions & Penalties Under the Amended PBPT Act
bullets: Genuine Family/Fiduciary Exceptions: Property held by a Karta/member of an HUF for family benefit from known sources, property held in a fiduciary capacity (trustee, executor, partner), or property purchased in the name of spouse or child out of known legal sources of income are excluded.
Penalties: Beyond confiscation without compensation, persons guilty of benami transactions face rigorous imprisonment of 1 to 7 years plus a fine up to 25% of the fair market value of the property.

inNews.source: Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) / LiveLaw
inNews.headline: Benami Prohibition Units Step Up Provisional Attachments Across Urban Real Estate and Shell Entities
inNews.relevance: CBDT enforcement reviews in October 2026 noted accelerated adjudication and confirmation of provisional attachments under the PBPT Act across high-value urban land parcels held in the names of unaware proxies.

statementBreakdown.explanation: Under Section 2(9)(A)(c), a transaction or arrangement in respect of a property where the owner of the property is not aware of, or denies knowledge of, such ownership is explicitly defined as a 'benami transaction'—not exempted from it.
Section 5 mandates that any property which is the subject matter of a benami transaction shall be liable to be confiscated by the Central Government without any compensation.

The amended Act establishes four authorities (Initiating Officer, Approving Authority, Administrator, and Adjudicating Authority) and explicitly creates a two-tier appellate mechanism: appeals from the Adjudicating Authority lie before the Appellate Tribunal (Section 30), with further appeal on substantial questions of law to the High Court (Section 49).

rows: Not benami if owner is unaware of transaction
Section 2(9)(A)(c): Owner unaware/denying ownership IS explicitly benami
Section 5 & Section 27: Confiscated by Central Government without compensation
Four authorities (IO, AA, Administrator, Adjudicating Authority) + Appellate Tribunal & High Court

hook.headline: If someone buys property in your name without telling you, does that escape the Benami Act?
hook.teaser: Notice how UPSC pairs a reversed statutory definition with a classic 'does not provide for any appellate mechanism' trap.

keywords.term: not treated as a benami transaction if the owner of the property is not aware
keywords.calloutTerm: “not treated as a benami transaction if the owner... is not aware”
keywords.calloutNote: The 2016 Benami Amendment says the exact opposite—buying property in the name of an unaware proxy is explicitly a benami transaction.
activePhrases: not treated as a benami transaction if the owner of the property is not aware

keywords.term: does not provide for any appellate mechanism
keywords.calloutTerm: “does not provide for any appellate mechanism”
keywords.calloutNote: Confiscating property without an appeal route would violate natural justice—the Act sets up four authorities plus an Appellate Tribunal and High Court appeal.
activePhrases: does not provide for any appellate mechanism
dimmedPhrases: not treated as a benami transaction if the owner of the property is not aware
contextPhrases: liable for confiscation by the Government

verdicts.source: Under Section 2(9)(A)(c), a transaction where the ostensible owner is unaware of or denies ownership is explicitly treated as a benami transaction.
Section 5 makes any property held benami liable to confiscation by the Central Government without compensation.
The Act provides four authorities and a full appellate mechanism through the Appellate Tribunal and the High Court.

answer.label: B
answer.text: Unaware-owner deals are explicitly benami and full Tribunal-to-High-Court appeals exist—so 2 only is the right answer.

subject: Economy
stem:
Which of the following are the objectives of 'National Nutrition Mission'?
1. To create awareness relating to malnutrition among pregnant women and lactating mothers.
2. To reduce the incidence of anaemia among young children, adolescent girls and women.
3. To promote the consumption of millets, coarse cereals and unpolished rice.
4. To promote the consumption of poultry eggs.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:

keywords.shortNote: India's flagship multi-ministerial convergence mission implemented by the Ministry of Women and Child Development (now integrated under Saksham Anganwadi and POSHAN 2.0) to curb stunting, undernutrition, anaemia, and low birth weight in a time-bound manner.
keywords.concept: National Nutrition Mission (POSHAN Abhiyaan): India's flagship multi-ministerial convergence mission implemented by the Ministry of Women and Child Development (now integrated under Saksham Anganwadi and POSHAN 2.0) to curb stunting, undernutrition, anaemia, and low birth weight in a time-bound manner.

keywords.shortNote: The community mobilization pillar of the National Nutrition Mission—featuring Rashtriya Poshan Maah (September) and Poshan Pakhwada (March)—designed to build awareness on maternal nutrition, breastfeeding, and complementary feeding among pregnant women and lactating mothers.
keywords.concept: Jan Andolan (Social & Behavioural Change Communication): The community mobilization pillar of the National Nutrition Mission—featuring Rashtriya Poshan Maah (September) and Poshan Pakhwada (March)—designed to build awareness on maternal nutrition, breastfeeding, and complementary feeding among pregnant women and lactating mothers.

keywords.shortNote: Core anthropometric indicators targeted by the National Nutrition Mission: stunting (low height-for-age reflecting chronic undernutrition), wasting (low weight-for-height reflecting acute undernutrition), and low birth weight (birth weight below 2,500 grams).
keywords.concept: Stunting, Wasting & Low Birth Weight: Core anthropometric indicators targeted by the National Nutrition Mission: stunting (low height-for-age reflecting chronic undernutrition), wasting (low weight-for-height reflecting acute undernutrition), and low birth weight (birth weight below 2,500 grams).

optionBreakdown.label: a
optionBreakdown.explanation: Maternal malnutrition awareness and reducing anaemia among children, adolescent girls, and women are core objectives of the National Nutrition Mission, whereas Statements 3 and 4 introduce specific food-commodity promotions absent from the Mission's charter.

optionBreakdown.label: b
optionBreakdown.explanation: Eliminated because promoting millets, coarse cereals, and unpolished rice is not an objective of the National Nutrition Mission.

optionBreakdown.label: c
optionBreakdown.explanation: Eliminated because promoting poultry egg consumption is not part of the central Mission's objectives.

optionBreakdown.label: d
optionBreakdown.explanation: Eliminated because both commodity-promotion statements are distractors while the two actual objectives (1 and 2) are omitted.

valueAddition.title: Four Quantifiable Targets & Four Pillars of National Nutrition Mission
bullets: Four Core Annual Reduction Targets: Reduce stunting in children (0–6 years) by 2% per annum, reduce undernutrition (underweight prevalence) by 2% per annum, reduce low birth weight by 2% per annum, and reduce anaemia among young children, adolescent girls, and women by 3% per annum.

Four Operational Pillars: (1) Inter-sectoral convergence across ministries (MWCD, Health, Jal Shakti, Rural Development), (2) ICT-based real-time growth monitoring via the Poshan Tracker app, (3) Intensified health and nutrition services during the first 1,000 days, and (4) Jan Andolan community mobilization.

valueAddition.title: Consolidation into Saksham Anganwadi and POSHAN 2.0
bullets: Integrated Umbrella Scheme: During the 15th Finance Commission cycle, POSHAN Abhiyaan was merged with Anganwadi Services and the Scheme for Adolescent Girls into 'Saksham Anganwadi and POSHAN 2.0' under the Ministry of Women and Child Development to combat malnutrition holistically.

inNews.source: Ministry of Women and Child Development (MWCD) / Press Information Bureau (PIB)
inNews.headline: Rashtriya Poshan Maah 2026 mobilizes over 10 crore beneficiaries across Anganwadi centres focusing on maternal nutrition, anaemia eradication, and Poshan Tracker growth monitoring
inNews.relevance: September 2026 Rashtriya Poshan Maah nationwide drives reinforced maternal awareness during the first 1,000 days and real-time growth and anaemia tracking across over 13.9 lakh Anganwadi centres under POSHAN 2.0.

statementBreakdown.reference: MWCD National Nutrition Mission · Jan Andolan & Maternal Awareness Pillar
statementBreakdown.explanation: Creating nutrition awareness and driving behavioural change among pregnant women, lactating mothers, and families during the critical first 1,000 days of a child's life is a foundational objective of the National Nutrition Mission.

statementBreakdown.reference: National Nutrition Mission Quantifiable Targets · Anaemia Reduction
statementBreakdown.explanation: Reducing the prevalence of anaemia among young children (6–59 months), adolescent girls, and women of reproductive age (15–49 years) by 3% per annum is one of the four core quantitative targets of the National Nutrition Mission.

statementBreakdown.reference: National Food Security Mission (NFSM) · Nutri-Cereals Sub-Mission
statementBreakdown.explanation: Promoting production and consumption of millets and coarse cereals falls under the Ministry of Agriculture's National Food Security Mission (Sub-Mission on Nutri-Cereals), not the stated objectives of the National Nutrition Mission.

statementBreakdown.reference: No Central Mandate for Poultry Egg Promotion
statementBreakdown.explanation: Promoting poultry egg consumption is not an official objective of the central National Nutrition Mission (Supplementary Nutrition Programme menus are decided locally by State Governments).

visualSuggestion.title: National Nutrition Mission (POSHAN Abhiyaan) — Official Targets vs. Non-Objectives

rows: Jan Andolan awareness for pregnant women & lactating mothers (Statement 1)
Reduce anaemia by 3% p.a. among children, adolescent girls & women (Statement 2)
States decide local Supplementary Nutrition menus; central mission sets calorie/protein norms

hook.headline: Does the National Nutrition Mission have specific targets to promote millets and poultry eggs?
hook.teaser: No—spot the two food-commodity distractors in Statements 3 and 4 to lock in Option (a).

keywords.term: anaemia among young children, adolescent girls and women
keywords.calloutNote: Reducing anaemia by 3% per year among young children, adolescent girls, and women is an explicit quantitative target of the National Nutrition Mission.
activePhrases: anaemia among young children, adolescent girls and women

keywords.calloutNote: The central National Nutrition Mission focuses on anthropometric targets and maternal awareness—not promoting specific foods like poultry eggs or millets.
activePhrases: consumption of poultry eggs
dimmedPhrases: anaemia among young children, adolescent girls and women

verdicts.source: Creating awareness on malnutrition among pregnant women and lactating mothers is a core pillar of the National Nutrition Mission.
Reducing anaemia among young children, adolescent girls, and women is one of the Mission's four quantitative goals.
Promoting millets and coarse cereals belongs to the Agriculture Ministry's National Food Security Mission, not the National Nutrition Mission.
Promoting poultry egg consumption is not an official objective of the central National Nutrition Mission.

answer.label: A
answer.text: Statements 1 and 2 only are correct—the Mission targets maternal malnutrition awareness and anaemia reduction, not promoting millets or poultry eggs.

valueAddition.subtitle: Add these to your Nutrition & Social Sector notes

items.desc: Cut stunting by 2%, underweight by 2%, low birth weight by 2%, and anaemia by 3% per annum.

items.title: Critical Window Focus
items.desc: Concentrates interventions from conception through a child's second birthday to prevent irreversible stunting.

items.title: Umbrella Integration
items.desc: Merged with Anganwadi Services and Adolescent Girls Scheme into Saksham Anganwadi and POSHAN 2.0.

subject: Economy
stem: The term 'Domestic Content Requirement' is sometimes seen in the news with reference to

options.text: Developing solar power production in our country
options.label: a

options.text: Granting licences to foreign T.V. channels in our country
options.label: b

options.text: Exporting our food products to other countries
options.label: c

options.text: Permitting foreign educational institutions to set up their campuses in our country
options.label: d

keywords.shortNote: A policy mandate under India's National Solar Mission requiring solar power developers to use domestically manufactured solar cells and modules to qualify for government power-purchase agreements.
keywords.concept: Domestic Content Requirement (DCR): A policy mandate under India's National Solar Mission requiring solar power developers to use domestically manufactured solar cells and modules to qualify for government power-purchase agreements.

keywords.shortNote: A core WTO non-discrimination obligation requiring imported products to be accorded treatment no less favourable than like domestic products regarding internal laws and procurement rules.
keywords.concept: National Treatment (GATT Article III:4): A core WTO non-discrimination obligation requiring imported products to be accorded treatment no less favourable than like domestic products regarding internal laws and procurement rules.

keywords.term: Approved List of Models and Manufacturers (ALMM)
keywords.shortNote: A non-tariff quality and supply-chain verification mechanism operated by the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE) that replaced direct WTO-challenged DCR mandates for government-backed solar projects.
keywords.concept: Approved List of Models and Manufacturers (ALMM): A non-tariff quality and supply-chain verification mechanism operated by the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE) that replaced direct WTO-challenged DCR mandates for government-backed solar projects.

optionBreakdown.label: a
optionBreakdown.reference: National Solar Mission & WTO Dispute DS456
optionBreakdown.explanation: Under the Jawaharlal Nehru National Solar Mission, India mandated that solar developers source solar cells and modules locally under DCR clauses, triggering a high-profile WTO dispute brought by the United States.

optionBreakdown.label: b
optionBreakdown.explanation: Foreign TV channel licensing is governed by uplinking and downlinking norms and FDI equity caps, not Domestic Content Requirement clauses.

optionBreakdown.label: c
optionBreakdown.explanation: Food exports are governed by importing countries' Sanitary and Phytosanitary (SPS) norms and Codex standards, not DCR rules.

optionBreakdown.label: d
optionBreakdown.reference: UGC Foreign Higher Educational Institutions Regulations
optionBreakdown.explanation: Foreign university campuses are regulated under UGC academic, infrastructure, and repatriation rules, unrelated to DCR.

valueAddition.title: The India–US WTO Solar Dispute (DS456)
bullets: The Dispute: The United States challenged India's DCR mandates under Phases I and II of the Jawaharlal Nehru National Solar Mission, arguing they discriminated against imported U.S. solar cells.

The Verdict: Both the WTO Panel and Appellate Body (2016) ruled against India, holding that DCR violated GATT Article III:4 (National Treatment) and TRIMs Article 2.1, while rejecting India's defence under the GATT Article III:8(a) government procurement exemption.

valueAddition.title: How India Pivoted After Losing the DCR Case
bullets: Phase-Out of Direct DCR: India withdrew mandatory DCR rules for private commercial solar bids and shifted toward WTO-compliant industrial support tools.

Modern Instruments: India now builds domestic solar manufacturing through Basic Customs Duty (BCD) on imported cells/modules, the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme for High-Efficiency Solar PV Modules, and the Approved List of Models and Manufacturers (ALMM).

inNews.source: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE) / Press Information Bureau
inNews.headline: MNRE extends Approved List of Models and Manufacturers (ALMM) mandate to solar PV cells alongside modules from 2026
inNews.relevance: MNRE's October 2026 solar manufacturing updates enforced domestic cell sourcing under ALMM List-II and PLI tranches, achieving the original DCR goal of curbing import reliance without reviving WTO-prohibited local-content clauses.

Struck down by WTO (violated GATT Art. III:4 & TRIMs)
Financial incentives linked to incremental sales of domestic PV modules
Designed within domestic subsidy rules (though scrutinized under ASCM)
Tariff protection + technical quality enlistment for public projects
Operates via bound tariff space & quality standards

hook.teaser: Think of the green energy mission where India tried forcing developers to buy locally made panels.

activePhrases: 'Domestic Content Requirement'

keywords.calloutNote: The US challenged India's DCR policy at the WTO, leading the Appellate Body to rule against India under GATT and TRIMs.

Foreign TV channel permissions depend on I&B Ministry guidelines and FDI limits, not DCR clauses.
Food exports deal with Sanitary and Phytosanitary quality rules, not domestic content mandates.
Foreign university campuses are regulated by UGC norms rather than Domestic Content Requirements.

answer.label: A
answer.text: Domestic Content Requirement refers to rules mandating locally manufactured cells and modules in India's solar power sector.

subject: Economy
stem: Who among the following can join the National Pension System (NPS)?

options.text: Persons of age from 21 to 55 only
options.label: b

options.text: All State Government employees joining the services after the date of notification by the respective State Governments
options.label: c

options.text: All Central Government employees including those of Armed Forces joining the services on or after 1st April, 2004
options.label: d

keywords.shortNote: A defined-contribution retirement savings scheme regulated by the Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA), introduced for Central Government recruits joining on or after 1 January 2004 (excluding Armed Forces) and subsequently opened to State Governments, corporates, and all citizens aged 18–70.
keywords.concept: National Pension System (NPS): A defined-contribution retirement savings scheme regulated by the Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA), introduced for Central Government recruits joining on or after 1 January 2004 (excluding Armed Forces) and subsequently opened to State Governments, corporates, and all citizens aged 18–70.

keywords.term: Defined Contribution vs. Defined Benefit Pension
keywords.shortNote: Under NPS's defined-contribution model, retirement corpus depends on regular employee-employer contributions and market-linked returns—replacing the fiscal liability of the unfunded defined-benefit Old Pension Scheme (OPS).
keywords.concept: Defined Contribution vs. Defined Benefit Pension: Under NPS's defined-contribution model, retirement corpus depends on regular employee-employer contributions and market-linked returns—replacing the fiscal liability of the unfunded defined-benefit Old Pension Scheme (OPS).

keywords.term: Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA)
keywords.shortNote: The statutory pension regulator established under the PFRDA Act, 2013 under the Ministry of Finance to regulate, promote, and ensure orderly growth of the National Pension System and Atal Pension Yojana (APY).
keywords.concept: Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA): The statutory pension regulator established under the PFRDA Act, 2013 under the Ministry of Finance to regulate, promote, and ensure orderly growth of the National Pension System and Atal Pension Yojana (APY).

optionBreakdown.label: a
optionBreakdown.reference: PFRDA All Citizen Model · NRIs & OCIs Eligible
optionBreakdown.explanation: NPS is not restricted to 'Resident Indian citizens only'—Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) and Overseas Citizens of India (OCIs) are also eligible to open and contribute to NPS accounts.

optionBreakdown.label: b
optionBreakdown.reference: PFRDA Entry Age Norm · 18 to 70 Years
optionBreakdown.explanation: The eligible entry age bracket under the NPS All Citizen Model is 18 to 70 years (18–65 years in 2017, later raised to 70 years)—not 21 to 55 years.

optionBreakdown.label: c
optionBreakdown.reference: PFRDA State Government Sector Model · Notification-Based Adoption
optionBreakdown.explanation: State Governments notify their own respective cut-off dates for adopting NPS, making it applicable to State Government employees joining service on or after the date notified by their respective State Government.

optionBreakdown.label: d
optionBreakdown.reference: Central Government Notification · Excludes Armed Forces & Effective 1st January 2004
optionBreakdown.explanation: NPS became mandatory for Central Government employees joining on or after 1st January 2004 (not 1st April 2004) and explicitly excludes the Armed Forces (Army, Navy, and Air Force).

valueAddition.title: Eligibility & Key Rules Across NPS Segments
bullets: Government Sector: Mandatory for Central Government employees (excluding Armed Forces) joining on or after 1 January 2004; applicable to State Government employees from the cut-off date notified by each respective State (every State except West Bengal notified NPS, though a few later reverted to OPS).

All Citizen & Corporate Models: Open to any Indian citizen (Resident, NRI, or OCI) aged 18 to 70 years, as well as minors under the NPS Vatsalya scheme (launched in 2024, converting into a regular NPS account at age 18).

valueAddition.title: NPS Exit Rules & Unified Pension Scheme (UPS) Update
bullets: Normal Exit at Superannuation / Age 60: Up to 60% of the accumulated pension corpus can be withdrawn tax-free as a lump sum, while at least 40% must be utilized to purchase an annuity from an IRDAI-regulated insurer for regular monthly pension.

Unified Pension Scheme (UPS, effective April 2025): Introduced as an optional assured-pension framework within the NPS architecture for Central Government employees—guaranteeing 50% of average basic pay drawn over the last 12 months before superannuation after 25 years of qualifying service.

inNews.source: Ministry of Finance / Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA)
inNews.headline: PFRDA reports NPS and Atal Pension Yojana total subscriber base crossing 8 crore with assets under management exceeding Rs. 13.5 lakh crore
inNews.relevance: October 2026 PFRDA subscriber and AUM disclosures highlighted strong voluntary adoption under the All Citizen Model, NPS Vatsalya minor accounts, and operationalization of the Unified Pension Scheme option for government employees.

hook.teaser: Spot two sharp errors in Option (d)—NPS excludes the Armed Forces and began on 1st January 2004, not 1st April.

keywords.calloutNote: Double error—NPS explicitly excludes the Armed Forces and took effect for Central recruits from 1st January 2004, not 1st April 2004.

The eligible entry age for joining NPS under the All Citizen Model is 18 to 70 years, not 21 to 55.

NPS excludes the Armed Forces and started for Central Government recruits on 1st January 2004, not 1st April 2004.

answer.label: C
answer.text: State Government employees joining after the date notified by their respective State Governments can join NPS, whereas Central NPS began on 1st January 2004 and excludes the Armed Forces.

subject: Economy
stem:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Standard Mark of Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) is mandatory for automotive tyres and tubes.
2. AGMARK is a quality Certification Mark issued by the Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO).
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

keywords.shortNote: India's national standards body operating under the Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution via the BIS Act, 2016, responsible for product standardization, ISI hallmarking, and mandatory Quality Control Orders.
keywords.concept: Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS): India's national standards body operating under the Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution via the BIS Act, 2016, responsible for product standardization, ISI hallmarking, and mandatory Quality Control Orders.

keywords.shortNote: A statutory quality certification mark administered in India by the Directorate of Marketing and Inspection (DMI) under the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare pursuant to the Agricultural Produce (Grading and Marking) Act, 1937.
keywords.concept: AGMARK: A statutory quality certification mark administered in India by the Directorate of Marketing and Inspection (DMI) under the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare pursuant to the Agricultural Produce (Grading and Marking) Act, 1937.

keywords.shortNote: A mandatory notification issued by the Government of India requiring specified goods—such as automotive tyres, cement, steel, and household electrical appliances—to conform to Indian Standards and bear the BIS Standard Mark before manufacture, import, or sale.
keywords.concept: Quality Control Order (QCO): A mandatory notification issued by the Government of India requiring specified goods—such as automotive tyres, cement, steel, and household electrical appliances—to conform to Indian Standards and bear the BIS Standard Mark before manufacture, import, or sale.

optionBreakdown.label: a
optionBreakdown.explanation: BIS certification is mandatory for automotive tyres and tubes under India's Quality Control Orders, whereas AGMARK is issued by India's Directorate of Marketing and Inspection rather than the FAO.

optionBreakdown.label: b
optionBreakdown.explanation: Eliminated because AGMARK is an Indian statutory mark under the 1937 Act, not an FAO international standard.

optionBreakdown.label: c
optionBreakdown.explanation: Eliminated because Statement 2 wrongly attributes AGMARK to the Food and Agriculture Organisation.

optionBreakdown.label: d
optionBreakdown.explanation: Eliminated because automotive tyres and tubes fall under BIS's mandatory certification regime for road safety.

valueAddition.title: India's Major Quality Certification Marks & Issuing Bodies
bullets: ISI Mark (BIS): Mandatory for safety-critical industrial and consumer goods notified under Quality Control Orders—such as automotive tyres and tubes, LPG cylinders, cement, steel products, helmets, and packaged drinking water.

AGMARK (Directorate of Marketing & Inspection): Covers over 220 agricultural, horticultural, and livestock commodities (pulses, spices, honey, vegetable oils, ghee); voluntary for domestic trade except where mandated under FSSAI regulations.

FPO Mark & FSSAI: FPO (Fruit Products Order) mark is mandatory for processed fruit products (jams, squashes, pickles) and is now enforced by the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.

valueAddition.title: Why BIS Mandatory QCOs Matter for Trade Policy
bullets: Safety & Non-Tariff Quality Shield: Mandatory BIS Quality Control Orders prevent substandard imports from dumping into Indian markets while raising domestic manufacturing compliance to global benchmarks.

statementBreakdown.reference: Pneumatic Tyres and Tubes for Automotive Vehicles (Quality Control) Order · BIS Mandatory Certification
statementBreakdown.explanation: Under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry's Quality Control Order, automotive pneumatic tyres and tubes cannot be manufactured, imported, stored, or sold in India unless they conform to Indian Standards and carry the mandatory BIS Standard (ISI) Mark.

statementBreakdown.reference: Agricultural Produce (Grading and Marking) Act, 1937 · Directorate of Marketing & Inspection (DMI)
statementBreakdown.explanation: AGMARK is a domestic Indian certification mark issued by the Directorate of Marketing and Inspection (DMI) under the Union Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare—not by the UN's Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO).

subject: Economy
stem:
What is the purpose of setting up of Small Finance Banks (SFBs) in India?
1. To supply credit to small business units.
2. To supply credit to small and marginal farmers.
3. To encourage young entrepreneurs to set up business particularly in rural areas.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:

keywords.shortNote: A niche category of differentiated commercial banks licensed under Section 22 of the Banking Regulation Act, 2049 to deliver basic savings vehicles and supply credit to unserved and underserved segments.
keywords.concept: Small Finance Banks (SFBs): A niche category of differentiated commercial banks licensed under Section 22 of the Banking Regulation Act, 2049 to deliver basic savings vehicles and supply credit to unserved and underserved segments.

keywords.shortNote: Banks tailored to specific market niches and customer cohorts—such as SFBs and Payments Banks—operating under customized regulatory mandates unlike universal commercial banks.
keywords.concept: Differentiated Banks: Banks tailored to specific market niches and customer cohorts—such as SFBs and Payments Banks—operating under customized regulatory mandates unlike universal commercial banks.

optionBreakdown.label: a
optionBreakdown.reference: Statements 1 and 2 are true; Statement 3 is false.
optionBreakdown.explanation: Correctly pairs the two explicit credit delivery mandates mandated in the RBI licensing circular.

optionBreakdown.label: b
optionBreakdown.explanation: Fails because statement 3 is a generic scheme objective rather than an SFB regulatory mandate.

optionBreakdown.label: c
optionBreakdown.explanation: Fails because it incorporates the uncodified entrepreneurial development distractor.

optionBreakdown.label: d
optionBreakdown.explanation: Fails because it mistakes an overarching developmental aim for a formal central bank licensing objective.

valueAddition.title: SFB Regulatory Framework & Mandates
bullets: Genesis: Recommended by the Committee on Comprehensive Financial Services for Small Businesses and Low Income Households (Nachiket Mor Committee, 2014).
Priority Sector Lending (PSL): SFBs are mandated to extend 75% of their Adjusted Net Bank Credit (ANBC) to priority sectors, compared to 40% for universal commercial banks.
Loan Ticket Size Cap: At least 50% of an SFB's loan portfolio must comprise loans and advances of up to Rs 25 lakh.
Branch Distribution: SFBs must open at least 25% of their total banking branches in unbanked rural centres (population up to 9,999).

valueAddition.title: SFBs vs Universal Banks vs Payments Banks
bullets: Lending Powers: SFBs engage in full basic banking, including lending and accepting both demand and time deposits, whereas Payments Banks cannot lend or issue credit cards.
Capital Adequacy: SFBs must maintain a minimum Capital to Risk-Weighted Assets Ratio (CRAR) of 15% on a continuous basis (compared to 9% for universal scheduled commercial banks).
On-Tap Licensing: Minimum paid-up voting equity capital for setting up an SFB is Rs 200 crore (Rs 300 crore for primary urban cooperative banks transitioning to SFB).

inNews.source: Reserve Bank of India
inNews.headline: RBI issues updated criteria for voluntary transition of Small Finance Banks to Universal Banks
inNews.relevance: Directly updates the regulatory lifecycle of SFBs tested in this PYQ, establishing operational track record, scheduled bank status, and minimum CRAR thresholds required for an SFB to graduate into a full universal bank.

statementBreakdown.reference: RBI Licensing Guidelines for SFBs (2014) · Paragraph 1
statementBreakdown.explanation: A primary codified objective of setting up SFBs is the supply of credit to small business units, micro and small enterprises, and unorganised sector entities through high-technology-low-cost operations.

statementBreakdown.reference: RBI Licensing Guidelines for SFBs (2014) · Paragraph 1
statementBreakdown.explanation: The explicit statutory guidelines frame the second core objective as providing credit to small and marginal farmers who lack access to formal banking channels.

Encouraging young rural entrepreneurs is a general economic policy objective served by specialized schemes (like Start-up India or Stand-Up India), but is not an institutional charter objective specified by the RBI for licensing SFBs.

hook.headline: Were Small Finance Banks created to fund young entrepreneurs?
hook.teaser: Statement 3 sounds completely reasonable, which is why thousands of aspirants fell for it.

keywords.term: supply credit to small business units
keywords.calloutNote: This is one of the two core licensing objectives explicitly specified by the RBI in 2014.
activePhrases: To supply credit to small business units.

keywords.calloutNote: A classic UPSC distractor: a government scheme goal disguised as a central bank banking license objective.
activePhrases: To encourage young entrepreneurs to set up business particularly in rural areas.
dimmedPhrases: To supply credit to small business units.
contextPhrases: setting up of Small Finance Banks (SFBs)

verdicts.source: The RBI 2014 licensing norms explicitly state that SFBs are created to supply credit to small business units and the unorganized sector.
Supplying credit to small and marginal farmers is explicitly specified as a primary objective under the RBI framework.
Fostering young rural entrepreneurs is a general policy goal of government schemes, not an RBI licensing charter objective for SFBs.

answer.label: A
answer.text: Statements 1 and 2 are correct; SFBs were established to supply credit to small businesses and marginal farmers, not specifically to promote young entrepreneurs.

valueAddition.subtitle: Add these to your Differentiated Banking notes

items.desc: SFBs must allocate 75% of adjusted net bank credit to priority sectors, nearly double the 40% target for universal banks.

items.desc: At least 50% of an SFB's total loan portfolio must consist of ticket sizes up to Rs 25 lakh.

subject: Economy
stem:
Which of the following statements is/are correct regarding the 'Monetary Policy Committee (MPC)?
1. It decides the RBI's benchmark interest rates.
2. It is a 12-member body including the Governor of RBI and is reconstituted every year.
3. It functions under the chairmanship of the Union Finance Minister.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:

keywords.shortNote: A statutory committee constituted under Section 45ZB of the RBI Act, 1934 that determines the policy repo rate required to achieve the inflation target.
keywords.concept: Monetary Policy Committee (MPC): A statutory committee constituted under Section 45ZB of the RBI Act, 1934 that determines the policy repo rate required to achieve the inflation target.

keywords.shortNote: A monetary policy framework legally anchoring CPI inflation at 4% with a tolerance band of +/- 2%, reviewed by the Central Government every five years.
keywords.concept: Flexible Inflation Targeting (FIT): A monetary policy framework legally anchoring CPI inflation at 4% with a tolerance band of +/- 2%, reviewed by the Central Government every five years.

optionBreakdown.label: a
optionBreakdown.reference: Statement 1 is true; Statements 2 and 3 are false.
optionBreakdown.explanation: Only Statement 1 accurately captures the statutory mandate of setting policy benchmark rates.

optionBreakdown.label: b
optionBreakdown.explanation: Fails because the committee has 6 members with 4-year external tenures, not 12 members reconstituted annually.

optionBreakdown.label: c
optionBreakdown.explanation: Fails because the RBI Governor chairs the committee, not the Union Finance Minister.

optionBreakdown.label: d
optionBreakdown.explanation: Fails because both statements contain factual errors regarding size, tenure, and chairmanship.

valueAddition.title: MPC Composition & Voting Rules
bullets: Six-Member Structure: 3 RBI members (RBI Governor as Ex-Officio Chairperson, Deputy Governor in charge of monetary policy, and one RBI officer nominated by the Central Board) plus 3 external experts appointed by the Centre.
Voting & Casting Vote: Each member gets one vote; decisions are taken by majority. In the event of a tie, the RBI Governor has a second or casting vote under Section 45ZL(3).

Tenure: External members are appointed for a 4-year term by the Central Government on the recommendation of a Search-cum-Selection Committee headed by the Cabinet Secretary, and are not eligible for reappointment.

valueAddition.title: Meeting Mandates & Failure Protocols
bullets: Meeting Frequency: The MPC is legally required to meet at least four times a year, with a minimum quorum of four members, including at least one RBI officer.

Accountability Report: If average CPI inflation breaches the 2% to 6% band for three consecutive quarters, the RBI must submit a statutory failure report to the Central Government explaining reasons, remedial steps, and the projected timeline for recovery.
Core Trap: UPSC frequently conflates the fiscal authority (Finance Minister) with the monetary authority (RBI Governor) or doubles committee sizes to create distractors.

inNews.source: Reserve Bank of India / Ministry of Finance
inNews.headline: Central Government appoints three new external members to Monetary Policy Committee for four-year term
inNews.relevance: Directly links to the reconstitution provisions of Section 45ZB of the RBI Act tested in this PYQ, reiterating the 4-year non-renewable tenure of external members.

statementBreakdown.explanation: Under the amended RBI Act, the MPC determines the policy interest rate (Repo Rate) required to achieve the inflation target, replacing the earlier system where the RBI Governor held sole veto power.

The MPC consists of 6 members (3 internal from RBI and 3 external appointed by the Central Government), and external members hold office for a tenure of 4 years without re-eligibility, not reconstituted every year.
The Governor of the Reserve Bank of India is the ex-officio Chairperson of the MPC; the Union Finance Minister has no seat or role in the committee.

hook.headline: Does the Finance Minister chair the Monetary Policy Committee?
hook.teaser: Statements 2 and 3 look official, but contain elementary factual traps.

keywords.calloutNote: This is the core mandate of the MPC: setting the Repo Rate to anchor inflation.
activePhrases: It decides the RBI's benchmark interest rates.

keywords.term: chairmanship of the Union Finance Minister
keywords.calloutNote: A classic trap mixing fiscal and monetary authorities. The MPC is chaired by the RBI Governor.
activePhrases: functions under the chairmanship of the Union Finance Minister.
dimmedPhrases: It decides the RBI's benchmark interest rates.

verdicts.source: Under Section 45ZB of the RBI Act, the MPC is legally empowered to fix the benchmark repo rate.
The MPC has 6 members, not 12. External members hold office for 4 years without reappointment.
The RBI Governor is the ex-officio Chairperson; the Finance Minister has no seat on the MPC.

answer.label: A
answer.text: Only Statement 1 is correct; the MPC has 6 members chaired by the RBI Governor, not 12 members under the Finance Minister.

items.title: Governor's Tie-Breaker
items.desc: Decisions are by majority vote; in case of a tie, the RBI Governor exercises a second casting vote.

subject: Economy
stem: Which of the following is a most likely consequence of implementing the 'Unified Payments Interface (UPI)'?

options.text: Mobile wallets will not be necessary for online payments.
options.label: a

options.text: Digital currency will totally replace the physical currency in about two decades.
options.label: b

options.text: Direct transfer of subsidies to poor people will become very effective.
options.label: d

keywords.shortNote: An open-architecture instant real-time payment system developed by NPCI that enables direct bank-to-bank account transfers using a Virtual Payment Address (VPA).
keywords.concept: Unified Payments Interface (UPI): An open-architecture instant real-time payment system developed by NPCI that enables direct bank-to-bank account transfers using a Virtual Payment Address (VPA).

keywords.shortNote: Stored-value electronic payment tools where funds must be preloaded from a bank account before they can be used to purchase goods or settle bills.
keywords.concept: Prepaid Payment Instruments (PPIs / Mobile Wallets): Stored-value electronic payment tools where funds must be preloaded from a bank account before they can be used to purchase goods or settle bills.

optionBreakdown.label: a
optionBreakdown.explanation: UPI links directly to underlying bank accounts via a Virtual Payment Address (VPA), enabling immediate debit and credit without the intermediate step of preloading money into a proprietary prepaid mobile wallet.

optionBreakdown.label: b
optionBreakdown.explanation: A sweeping speculative claim; cash continues to coexist with digital payments due to informal sector realities, digital divides, and privacy preferences.

optionBreakdown.label: c
optionBreakdown.explanation: FDI decisions are determined by macroeconomic fundamentals, market size, regulatory stability, and ease of doing business, not retail payment rails.

optionBreakdown.label: d
optionBreakdown.explanation: DBT subsidy delivery was already anchored on the JAM Trinity through Aadhaar Payment Bridge (APB) and NEFT/NACH; UPI is an optional commercial interface, not the backbone infrastructure for welfare transfers.

valueAddition.title: UPI Architecture vs Mobile Wallets
bullets: Operational Difference: Wallets require two legs (bank to wallet, then wallet to merchant/peer); UPI operates on a single direct account-to-account settlement leg built on the Immediate Payment Service (IMPS).
Interoperability: Traditional closed/semi-closed wallets trapped balances within closed loops; UPI enables universal cross-app and cross-bank interoperability using a single VPA / UPI ID.
Interchange on PPI: Under RBI and NPCI rules, prepaid wallets can be loaded via UPI, with an interchange fee levied on merchant transactions conducted via PPIs on UPI rails.

valueAddition.title: Institutional Ecosystem of UPI
bullets: Governing Umbrella: Owned and operated by the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) under the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007.
Feature Enhancements: Evolved to include UPI AutoPay (recurring mandates), UPI Lite (on-device wallet for small offline/pinless transactions up to Rs 500), and UPI 123PAY for feature phones.
Credit Integration: RBI expanded UPI's scope beyond savings accounts to permit linking Rupay credit cards and pre-sanctioned credit lines from commercial banks.

inNews.source: Reserve Bank of India / NPCI
inNews.headline: RBI expands cross-border linkage of UPI with global real-time payment switches
inNews.relevance: Directly updates the global footprint of the retail payment rail tested in this PYQ, linking UPI with international fast-payment systems (such as Singapore's PayNow and UAE's AANI) for real-time bilateral remittances.
